### Guide

#### Common graph paper sizes

| Squares | Also called | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 mm, heavy every 1 cm | millimetre or metric graph paper | technical drawing, physics and chemistry graphs |
| 2 mm | fine metric grid | data plots, sewing and craft patterns |
| 5 mm | maths squares | school maths in much of Europe and Asia, notes, sketching |
| 1 cm | centimetre squares | primary maths, area and fractions, large charts |
| 1/4 inch | 4 squares per inch, “quad ruled” | US school maths and science |
| 1/5 inch | 5 squares per inch | engineering and computation pads |
| 1/10 inch | 10 squares per inch | precise data plots |

#### Ruled and handwriting paper

Handwriting paper has a solid top line, a dashed middle line and a solid baseline in each row, with room below for letters that hang down – the large size suits children who are learning to form letters.

| Ruling | Line spacing | Typical use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Narrow | 1/4 in (6.35 mm) | small handwriting, more lines per page |
| College ruled | 9/32 in (7.1 mm) | US college and high-school notebooks |
| A4 standard | 8 mm | exercise books in the UK, Europe and India |
| Wide ruled | 11/32 in (8.7 mm) | younger students, larger handwriting |

#### Which paper for what

- **Dot grid** – bullet journals, lettering and sketches where full lines would be too busy. 5 mm is the usual journal spacing.
- **Isometric** – drawings of 3D shapes, cubes and buildings: the lines run at 30° to the horizontal, so the three edges of a cube can be drawn along them.
- **Hexagon** – board-game and fantasy maps, organic chemistry rings, quilting and tiling patterns.
- **Polar** – plotting angles and directions, radar charts and polar equations, with rings for distance and rays every 5–30°.
- **Semi-log** – quantities that grow or decay exponentially (bacteria, interest, radioactive decay) plot as straight lines.
- **Log-log** – power laws such as y = x² or Kepler’s third law plot as straight lines.
- **Coordinate plane** – plotting points, lines and shapes in algebra and geometry classes.

#### Printing at true size

Printers can scale a page without asking: “Fit to page” or “Shrink to printable area” makes every square a few percent too small. The PDF asks PDF readers to print at actual size, but check the print dialog says **100%** or **Actual size**, then measure ten squares with a ruler.

Most printers cannot print in the outer 3–5 mm of the sheet, so keep a margin of at least that – the default is 10 mm.

### FAQ

**How do I print graph paper at the right size?**
Download the PDF and print it with the scale at **100%** or **Actual size** – not “Fit to page”. The PDF is drawn in exact millimetres and asks the printer not to scale it. Measure ten squares to check: ten 5 mm squares should be 5 cm.

**Is the graph paper free to use in class?**
Yes. Print as many copies as you need for home, school or work. There is no sign-up, no watermark and no limit.

**What size squares does normal graph paper have?**
It depends on where you are: 5 mm squares are common in Europe and India, 1/4 inch squares (four per inch) in the United States, and 1 mm millimetre paper with heavier lines every centimetre for technical work. All are presets here, or type any size.

**What is isometric graph paper?**
Paper with lines at 30° to the horizontal (and usually upright lines too), forming equilateral triangles. It makes it easy to draw 3D objects such as cubes, because their edges follow the grid. Choose **Dots** for isometric dot paper.

**What is semi-log paper used for?**
One axis is logarithmic and the other is ordinary. Anything that grows or shrinks by the same factor in equal times – population, compound interest, radioactive decay – plots as a straight line on it. Log-log paper makes power laws straight.

**Can I print a coordinate plane worksheet?**
Yes. Choose **Coordinate plane**, pick one to six planes per page, all four quadrants or the first, and how far the axes run. Turn on **Name & date** for a worksheet heading.

**Can I change the line colour?**
Choose blue, green, grey, orange-red or black, or **Custom** for any colour for the lines and the heavier lines. Light colours are easier on the eyes and stay in the background of what you draw.

## Car Loan EMI Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/car-loan-emi-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-16

Free car loan EMI calculator for India: EMI on the on-road price, the real cost of a flat rate, processing fee and APR, tenure comparison and early closure.

### At a glance

- Starts from the **on-road price**: ex-showroom price + RTO and road tax + insurance + accessories, less your down payment.
- Example: a ₹9.2 lakh loan at 9% for 5 years has an EMI of **₹19,098** and total interest of **₹2,25,861**.
- Converts a **flat rate** to the reducing-balance rate it really is: **7% flat for 5 years costs 12.50% a year**, 8% flat costs 14.13%.
- Adds the **processing fee with 18% GST** to the cost and shows the true yearly cost (APR) – a 0.5% fee lifts 9% to about 9.25%.
- **Compares 3- to 7-year loans** side by side: at 9%, stretching ₹9.2 lakh from 3 to 7 years halves the EMI but raises the interest from ₹1.33 lakh to ₹3.23 lakh.
- **Early closure**: the outstanding amount, the foreclosure charge with GST and what you save. RBI rules bar pre-payment charges on floating-rate loans to individuals sanctioned or renewed from 1 January 2026.
- Checks the **20/4/10 rule of thumb** and builds a full year-by-year and month-by-month schedule. Nothing you enter leaves your browser.

### Features

- **The whole price, not just the sticker**: Road tax, insurance and accessories add a good deal to the ex-showroom price. Enter them once and the loan follows.
- **See through flat rates**: A flat rate charges interest on the full loan for the whole term, so it looks about half as expensive as it is. The calculator shows the real rate to compare.
- **Fees count too**: The processing fee and its GST are added to the cost and folded into an APR, so offers with different fees compare fairly.
- **Pick a sensible tenure**: A table of 3- to 7-year loans shows how a smaller EMI trades against more interest. Tap a row to switch to it.
- **Plan an early close**: Choose when you might pay off the loan and the charge your lender takes, and see whether it is worth it.
- **Private**: Everything is worked out on your device. Your last figures are kept in this browser for next time.

### How to calculate your car loan EMI

1. **Enter the on-road price** — Type the ex-showroom price, RTO and road tax, insurance and accessories from the dealer’s quotation.
2. **Set your down payment** — Type an amount or tap 10%, 20% or 30%; the loan amount updates.
3. **Enter the rate and tenure** — Choose **Reducing balance** for a bank-quoted rate or **Flat** for a dealer’s flat rate, then pick 3–7 years.
4. **Add the processing fee** — Enter the fee as a % of the loan; GST is added at 18%.
5. **Read the result** — See the EMI, total interest, APR and total cost, compare tenures, and check what closing early would save.

### Guide

#### Car loan EMI formula

Banks work out a car loan EMI on the reducing balance: **EMI = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1)**, where P is the loan, r the monthly rate (annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n the number of months. Each EMI pays the month’s interest on what you still owe, and the rest reduces the loan.

With a **flat rate**, interest is worked out on the full loan for the whole term – P × rate × years – and added to the loan before dividing by the months. Because you are paying interest on money you have already repaid, a flat rate costs much more than the same number on a reducing balance.

| Flat rate | Tenure | Equivalent reducing rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6% | 3 years | 11.08% |
| 7% | 5 years | 12.50% |
| 7% | 7 years | 12.16% |
| 8% | 5 years | 14.13% |
| 9% | 5 years | 15.71% |

#### EMI for ₹9.2 lakh at 9% by tenure

A car loses value every year, so a long loan can leave you owing more than the car is worth. Keeping the tenure short keeps interest down and the loan below the car’s value.

| Tenure | EMI | Total interest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 3 years | ₹29,256 | ₹1,33,207 |
| 4 years | ₹22,894 | ₹1,78,923 |
| 5 years | ₹19,098 | ₹2,25,861 |
| 6 years | ₹16,583 | ₹2,74,012 |
| 7 years | ₹14,802 | ₹3,23,364 |

#### The 20/4/10 rule

A popular rule of thumb for buying a car: put down at least **20%**, borrow for no more than **4 years**, and keep the EMI – ideally all car costs, including fuel and insurance – within **10%** of your income. It is a guide rather than a rule, but it keeps a car affordable for the whole loan.

### FAQ

**How is car loan EMI calculated?**
With the reducing-balance formula EMI = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), where P is the loan amount, r the monthly interest rate and n the number of months. For ₹9.2 lakh at 9% a year for 60 months, r = 0.0075 and the EMI is ₹19,098.

**Is a flat interest rate cheaper?**
No – it only looks cheaper. A flat rate charges interest on the original loan for the whole term even as you repay it. A 7% flat rate over 5 years costs the same as 12.5% a year on a reducing balance. Choose **Flat** in the calculator to see the equivalent rate before you compare offers.

**Is the loan on the ex-showroom or the on-road price?**
Lenders fund a share of the car’s price – some of the ex-showroom price, others of the on-road price – and you pay the rest as a down payment. This calculator starts from the on-road price, the total you actually pay, so the down payment covers whatever the loan does not.

**Can I close my car loan early?**
Usually yes, after a minimum number of EMIs set by your lender, sometimes with a foreclosure charge on the outstanding amount plus GST. Car loans are often fixed-rate, so check your sanction letter. Under RBI’s pre-payment directions, floating-rate loans to individuals for non-business purposes sanctioned or renewed from 1 January 2026 carry no pre-payment charge.

**What is a good tenure for a car loan?**
Shorter is cheaper: the table shows that the same loan costs about 2.4 times as much interest over 7 years as over 3. Many people pick the shortest tenure whose EMI fits comfortably in their budget – often 4 or 5 years.

**Does the processing fee matter?**
Yes. A fee paid upfront means you borrow less than you repay on, which raises the true cost. The calculator adds 18% GST to the fee and shows the APR, so a lower rate with a high fee can be compared fairly with a higher rate and no fee.

2. **Set the rate and tenure** — Enter the interest rate and choose a tenure from 10 to 30 years, and the processing fee if any.
3. **Add prepayments** — Add an extra amount every month or year, or one-time prepayments, and choose whether they shorten the tenure or lower the EMI.
4. **Try a rate change** — Switch on **See a rate change** to see a floating rate move after a few years.
5. **Check tax and eligibility** — Pick your regime and slab for the tax saved, and enter your income to see the loan it supports.

### Guide

#### EMI on ₹50 lakh at 8.5% by tenure

Going from 20 to 30 years lowers the EMI by under ₹5,000 but adds over ₹34 lakh of interest. A longer tenure with regular prepayments keeps the EMI flexible while still cutting the cost.

| Tenure | EMI | Total interest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 years | ₹61,993 | ₹24,39,141 |
| 15 years | ₹49,237 | ₹38,62,656 |
| 20 years | ₹43,391 | ₹54,13,879 |
| 25 years | ₹40,261 | ₹70,78,406 |
| 30 years | ₹38,446 | ₹88,40,443 |

#### Reduce the EMI or the tenure?

When you prepay, lenders usually let you keep the EMI and finish sooner, or keep the end date and pay a smaller EMI. **Shortening the tenure saves far more interest**, because the whole EMI keeps working against a smaller balance. Lowering the EMI makes sense when you need breathing space in the monthly budget.

Under RBI’s pre-payment directions, floating-rate loans to individuals for non-business purposes sanctioned or renewed from 1 January 2026 cannot carry pre-payment charges, whatever the source of the money.

#### RBI loan-to-value limits

The rest is your down payment (margin). Stamp duty and registration are usually not counted in the property value for this, so plan for them separately.

| Loan amount | Largest loan as a share of the property value |
| --- | --- |
| Up to ₹30 lakh | 90% |
| Above ₹30 lakh up to ₹75 lakh | 80% |
| Above ₹75 lakh | 75% |

#### Home loan tax benefits

Each co-owner who also pays the EMIs can claim up to the limits separately. The Income-tax Act, 2025, in force from 1 April 2026, keeps these deductions under new section numbers.

| Deduction | Old regime | New regime |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Interest, self-occupied home (section 24(b)) | up to ₹2 lakh a year | not allowed |
| Principal repaid (section 80C) | within the ₹1.5 lakh 80C limit | not allowed |
| Interest, let-out home | against the rent; a loss up to ₹2 lakh can reduce other income | against that home’s rent only |

### FAQ

**How is home loan EMI calculated?**
EMI = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), where P is the loan, r the monthly interest rate (annual rate ÷ 12 ÷ 100) and n the number of months. ₹50 lakh at 8.5% for 240 months gives ₹43,391.

**Is it better to prepay or invest?**
Prepaying saves the loan’s interest rate with certainty, after tax. If you are in the old regime and still within the ₹2 lakh interest deduction, the saving is a little lower. Many borrowers do both – keep an emergency fund and investments going, and prepay windfalls such as bonuses.

**Should I reduce my EMI or tenure after prepaying?**
Reducing the tenure saves much more interest; reducing the EMI eases your monthly budget. Switch between **Shorten the tenure** and **Lower the EMI** in the calculator to see the difference for your loan.

**How much home loan can I get on my salary?**
Lenders typically let all your EMIs together take up 40–60% of your take-home pay. With ₹1 lakh a month and no other EMIs, 50% allows an EMI of ₹50,000 – about ₹57.6 lakh at 8.5% for 20 years. The property’s loan-to-value limit can cap it further.

**Can I claim home loan benefits in the new tax regime?**
Not for a home you live in: the new regime allows neither the interest deduction nor 80C for principal. For a let-out home, interest can still be set off against that home’s rental income.

**What happens when the repo rate changes?**
Repo-linked loans reset at intervals set in your agreement. Lenders usually keep the EMI and change the tenure; you can ask to change the EMI instead. Use **See a rate change** to compare both.

## Income Tax Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/income-tax-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-16

Free income tax calculator for India, FY 2026-27 and 2025-26: compare the new and old regimes with HRA, 80C, 80D, NPS and home loan, slab by slab.

### At a glance

- New-regime slabs for **FY 2026-27**, unchanged by Budget 2026: nil up to ₹4 lakh, then 5%, 10%, 15%, 20% and 25% in steps of ₹4 lakh, and **30% above ₹24 lakh**.
- No tax up to **₹12 lakh** of taxable income in the new regime thanks to the rebate (section 87A, section 156 of the 2025 Act) – a salary of **₹12.75 lakh** after the ₹75,000 standard deduction – with marginal relief just above.
- Old regime: nil up to ₹2.5 lakh (₹3 lakh at 60–79, ₹5 lakh at 80+), then 5%, 20% and 30%, with a rebate up to ₹5 lakh and a ₹50,000 standard deduction.
- **HRA** is the least of the HRA received, rent minus 10% of basic, and 50% of basic in metro cities (40% elsewhere). From FY 2026-27, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad join Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai at 50%.
- Old-regime deductions with their limits: 80C ₹1.5 lakh, NPS 80CCD(1B) ₹50,000, 80D, 80E, 80G, 80TTA/80TTB and home-loan interest up to ₹2 lakh. The new regime allows the employer’s NPS contribution up to 14% of basic.
- Surcharge of 10%, 15% and 25% (37% in the old regime above ₹5 crore) **with marginal relief**, and 4% health and education cess.
- Shows which regime is cheaper, by how much, and the **extra deductions the old regime would need** to break even. Everything stays in your browser.

### Features

- **Both regimes side by side**: Every figure is worked out under the new and the old regime at once, with the cheaper one marked and the difference in rupees.
- **The full working**: Gross income, exemptions, deductions, taxable income, slab-by-slab tax, rebate, marginal relief, surcharge and cess – line by line.
- **HRA done properly**: The three-way HRA rule with the right city rate for the year, including the four cities added to the 50% list from 2026-27.
- **Monthly or yearly**: Type your salary per month or per year, and see the tax per month to compare with the TDS on your payslip.
- **Break-even deductions**: If the new regime wins, see how much more you would need to invest or claim before the old regime would pay off.
- **Private**: Your salary and deductions never leave your device; they are kept in this browser for next time.

### How to calculate your income tax

1. **Choose the year and your age** — Pick FY 2026-27 or FY 2025-26, and your age group for the old-regime slabs.
2. **Enter your salary** — Type your gross salary, basic pay, HRA received and rent paid – per month or per year – and your city.
3. **Add other income** — Add interest, other income and any house property: home-loan interest, or rent from a let-out home.
4. **Add deductions** — Enter 80C, NPS, health insurance and other deductions; they count only in the old regime.
5. **Compare** — Read the tax under both regimes, which one is lower, and the full breakdown slab by slab.

### Guide

#### New tax regime slabs, FY 2025-26 and 2026-27

A rebate of up to ₹60,000 makes the tax nil when taxable income is ₹12 lakh or less. Just above ₹12 lakh, marginal relief caps the tax at the income above ₹12 lakh, until about ₹12.7 lakh.

| Taxable income | Rate |
| --- | --- |
| Up to ₹4,00,000 | Nil |
| ₹4,00,001 – ₹8,00,000 | 5% |
| ₹8,00,001 – ₹12,00,000 | 10% |
| ₹12,00,001 – ₹16,00,000 | 15% |
| ₹16,00,001 – ₹20,00,000 | 20% |
| ₹20,00,001 – ₹24,00,000 | 25% |
| Above ₹24,00,000 | 30% |

#### Old tax regime slabs

A rebate of up to ₹12,500 makes the tax nil when taxable income is ₹5 lakh or less.

| Taxable income | Below 60 | 60 to 79 | 80 and over |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Up to ₹2,50,000 | Nil | Nil | Nil |
| ₹2,50,001 – ₹3,00,000 | 5% | Nil | Nil |
| ₹3,00,001 – ₹5,00,000 | 5% | 5% | Nil |
| ₹5,00,001 – ₹10,00,000 | 20% | 20% | 20% |
| Above ₹10,00,000 | 30% | 30% | 30% |

#### New or old regime: tax on salary

With cess, for a resident under 60 with only salary income, using the standard deduction, ₹1.5 lakh under 80C and ₹25,000 under 80D in the old regime. Large HRA and home-loan claims can tip the balance – enter yours above.

| Salary | New regime | Old regime with ₹1.75 lakh of deductions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ₹8 lakh | ₹0 | ₹28,600 |
| ₹10 lakh | ₹0 | ₹70,200 |
| ₹12.75 lakh | ₹0 | ₹1,32,600 |
| ₹15 lakh | ₹97,500 | ₹2,02,800 |
| ₹20 lakh | ₹1,92,400 | ₹3,58,800 |
| ₹25 lakh | ₹3,19,800 | ₹5,14,800 |
| ₹30 lakh | ₹4,75,800 | ₹6,70,800 |

#### What changed in 2026

The **Income-tax Act, 2025** replaced the 1961 Act from 1 April 2026. It speaks of a single “tax year” instead of the previous year and assessment year, and renumbers the sections – the 87A rebate, for example, is now section 156 – but Budget 2026 kept the rates, the ₹12 lakh rebate limit and the ₹75,000 standard deduction.

Under the new Income-tax Rules, 2026, HRA in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad is worked out at 50% of salary, like Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai. For FY 2025-26 those four cities stay at 40%.

### FAQ

**Is income up to ₹12 lakh tax-free?**
In the new regime, yes: if your taxable income is ₹12 lakh or less, the rebate wipes out the tax. For salaried people, the ₹75,000 standard deduction makes a salary of up to ₹12.75 lakh tax-free. The rebate does not apply to income taxed at special rates, such as capital gains on shares.

**Which tax regime is better for me?**
It depends on your deductions. The new regime has lower rates but few deductions; the old one rewards large claims such as HRA, 80C, 80D and home-loan interest. Enter your figures and the calculator shows both totals, the cheaper regime and how much more you would need to claim for the old one to win.

**How is HRA exemption calculated?**
It is the least of three amounts: the HRA you receive; the rent you pay minus 10% of basic pay and DA; and 50% of basic and DA in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai – plus Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad from 2026-27 – or 40% elsewhere. It is available only in the old regime.

**Can I switch between the old and new regimes?**
If you have no business income, you can choose either regime every year when you file your return. Tell your employer your choice so that TDS is deducted correctly; the new regime applies if you do not.

**What is marginal relief?**
It stops a small rise in income from causing a bigger rise in tax. Just above ₹12 lakh in the new regime, your tax cannot be more than the income above ₹12 lakh. The same idea applies at the surcharge thresholds of ₹50 lakh, ₹1 crore, ₹2 crore and ₹5 crore.

**Does this calculator include capital gains?**
No. It covers salary, pension, house property, interest and other income taxed at slab rates for resident individuals. Gains on shares and mutual funds are taxed at special rates with their own rules, so add them separately or ask a tax professional.

## Student Loan Payoff & Refinance Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/student-loan-payoff-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-16

Free student loan payoff calculator: add every loan, pay extra with the avalanche or snowball method, see your debt-free date and test a refinance offer.

### At a glance

- Handles up to 15 loans, each with its own balance, APR and monthly payment, federal or private.
- Example: $40,000 across three loans at 5–9% on 10-year payments costs **$16,417** in interest; **$200 a month extra** with the avalanche method cuts that to **$9,073** and finishes **47 months sooner**.
- **Avalanche** puts the extra on the highest-rate loan first and always costs the least interest; **snowball** clears the smallest balance first. When a loan is paid off, its payment rolls on to the next.
- Shows your **debt-free date**, the month each loan is paid off and a combined year-by-year schedule you can download as CSV.
- **Refinance**: choose which loans to refinance and compare a new rate, term and fees with keeping them – monthly payment, total interest, lifetime saving and the months to recover any fees.
- Warns when federal loans are included: refinancing them with a private lender gives up income-driven repayment, Public Service Loan Forgiveness and federal deferment and forbearance.
- Interest is worked out monthly at APR ÷ 12. Nothing you enter leaves your browser.

### Features

- **All your loans together**: Federal and private loans with different rates and payments, in one plan with one debt-free date.
- **Avalanche or snowball**: Compare the interest-saving and the quick-wins approach on your own numbers.
- **Every extra dollar counted**: Add an extra monthly amount and see the interest saved and the months cut, loan by loan.
- **Honest refinancing**: A lower payment can still cost more over a longer term. The calculator shows both, with fees included.
- **Federal protections flagged**: Refinancing federal loans privately is permanent; the calculator says what you would give up.
- **Private**: No sign-up, no credit check and no data sent anywhere.

### How to plan your student loan payoff

1. **List your loans** — Enter each loan’s balance, APR and monthly payment from your servicer, and tick **Federal** for federal loans.
2. **Add an extra payment** — Type how much more you can pay each month, or tap a preset.
3. **Pick a method** — Choose **Highest rate** (avalanche) to save the most, or **Smallest balance** (snowball) for quick wins.
4. **Read your plan** — See your debt-free date, total interest, what you save and when each loan is paid off.
5. **Test a refinance** — On **Refinance**, tick the loans, enter the offer’s APR, term and fees, and compare.

### Guide

#### Avalanche or snowball?

Both methods pay every loan its normal payment and send any extra money to one loan at a time. **Avalanche** targets the highest interest rate, which is mathematically the cheapest. **Snowball** targets the smallest balance, so the first loan disappears sooner – a boost that helps some people keep going. On the example below the difference is small, so the best method is the one you will stick to.

| Extra a month | Debt-free in (avalanche) | Interest (avalanche) | Interest (snowball) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $0 | about 10 years | $16,417 | $16,417 |
| $100 | 7 years 7 months | $11,568 | $12,430 |
| $200 | 6 years 2 months | $9,073 | $9,842 |
| $500 | 4 years | $5,604 | $6,097 |

#### When refinancing makes sense

- You have **private loans** at a high rate and can qualify for a clearly lower one – the example’s $15,000 private loan at 9% costs $7,802 in interest over 10 years, but $4,535 at 5.5%.
- You will **keep or shorten the term**: stretching the term lowers the payment but can raise the total interest even at a lower rate.
- Any **fees** are repaid by the lower payments well before the loan ends.
- You do **not** need federal benefits – income-driven repayment, Public Service Loan Forgiveness, generous deferment and forbearance. Refinancing federal loans privately ends them for good.

### FAQ

**How do I pay off student loans faster?**
Pay more than the minimum and direct the extra to one loan at a time – the highest-rate loan saves the most interest. When that loan is gone, add its payment to the next. Ask your servicer to apply extra payments to principal on the loan you choose, not to future payments.

**Is it better to pay off the highest interest or the smallest balance first?**
Highest interest first (avalanche) always costs least. Smallest balance first (snowball) gives earlier wins. Try both in the calculator: with similar rates the difference is often a few hundred dollars.

**Should I refinance my federal student loans?**
Only after weighing what you give up. A private refinance can lower the rate, but the loans lose federal protections such as income-driven repayment, Public Service Loan Forgiveness and federal deferment and forbearance, and that cannot be reversed. Many borrowers refinance only their private loans.

**Does refinancing always save money?**
No. A lower rate over a longer term can cost more in total interest, and fees add to the cost. The calculator compares the lifetime cost of keeping your loans with the offer, fees included.

**How is student loan interest calculated?**
Most US student loans charge simple daily interest; this calculator uses the monthly equivalent, APR ÷ 12 on the balance, which gives very close results. Your servicer’s figures may differ by small amounts because of day counts and payment dates.

Free US mortgage calculator with PMI, property tax, home insurance and HOA: monthly payment, when PMI ends, amortization schedule and extra payments.

### At a glance

- Adds up the whole payment – **principal and interest, property tax, homeowners insurance, PMI and HOA** (PITI) – and shows each part.

- **Extra payments**: $200 a month more on the $320,000 loan saves **$105,429** of interest and pays it off **6 years 7 months** sooner – and lets you ask to drop PMI sooner.
- Checks the **28/36 guideline** and estimates the home price your income supports. Property tax can be a rate or a yearly amount.
- Full amortization schedule with a PMI column, by year or by month, as CSV. Nothing you enter leaves your browser.

### Features

- **The real monthly payment**: Lenders and listings often quote principal and interest only. Taxes, insurance, PMI and HOA can add hundreds a month – here they are all in.
- **PMI, start to finish**: The PMI payment, the month it ends – on request at 80% or automatically at 78% – and the total you will pay.
- **Pay it off sooner**: Add extra principal every month or once a year and see the interest saved and the years cut.
- **Affordability check**: Compare your payment with the 28/36 guideline and see the price that fits your income.
- **Amortization schedule**: Every payment split into principal, interest and PMI, with the balance left, by year or by month.
- **Private**: No sign-up and no lead forms: your numbers stay in your browser.

### How to calculate a mortgage payment

1. **Enter the home price and down payment** — Type the price, then the down payment in dollars or tap 3%, 5%, 10% or 20%.
2. **Set the rate and term** — Enter the interest rate and pick a 10-, 15-, 20- or 30-year term.
3. **Add taxes and insurance** — Enter the property tax rate or yearly amount, homeowners insurance and any HOA dues.
4. **Check PMI** — With under 20% down, enter the PMI rate from your quote and choose whether you will ask to cancel it at 80%.
5. **Read the result** — See the monthly payment and its parts, when PMI ends, the payoff date and the total cost; add extra payments to compare.

### Guide

#### What is in a mortgage payment

- **Principal and interest** – the loan payment itself: P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), with r the monthly rate and n the number of payments.
- **Property tax** – set by your county or city, usually paid through an escrow account with the mortgage.
- **Homeowners insurance** – required by lenders, also often paid through escrow.
- **PMI** – private mortgage insurance on conventional loans with less than 20% down; it protects the lender, not you.
- **HOA dues** – paid to a homeowners association, usually separately from the mortgage.

#### 15-year or 30-year mortgage

For a $320,000 loan at 6.5%. Shorter loans usually come with lower rates too, which widens the gap further. A 30-year loan with regular extra payments keeps the lower required payment while cutting much of the interest.

| Term | Principal & interest | Total interest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 15 years | $2,787.54 | $181,758 |
| 20 years | $2,385.83 | $252,600 |
| 30 years | $2,022.62 | $408,142 |

#### When PMI ends

Under the Homeowners Protection Act, for loans on a primary home made since July 1999: you may ask in writing to cancel PMI once the balance reaches **80% of the original value** (the lower of the price and the appraisal), if your payments are up to date. Extra payments bring that date forward. PMI **must end automatically** when the original schedule reaches **78%**, and in any case by the first month after the **midpoint** of the loan term if you are current. FHA mortgage insurance follows different rules.

### FAQ

**How is a mortgage payment calculated?**
The loan part uses P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1): P is the loan, r the yearly rate ÷ 12 and n the number of months. For $320,000 at 6.5% over 360 months that is $2,022.62. Property tax, insurance, PMI and HOA are then added on top.

**How do I avoid or get rid of PMI?**
Put down at least 20% on a conventional loan. If you put down less, you can ask to cancel PMI once the balance is 80% of the original value – sooner if you pay extra principal – and it ends by itself at 78%. A big rise in value can also help, but lenders usually require an appraisal for that.

**How much house can I afford?**
A common starting point is the 28/36 guideline: total housing costs within 28% of gross monthly income, and all debt payments within 36%. Enter your income and debts in the calculator to see the price that fits, then compare with what lenders approve.

**Are extra mortgage payments worth it?**
Every extra dollar of principal saves the loan’s interest rate on it for the rest of the loan. $200 a month more on a $320,000 loan at 6.5% saves about $105,000 and 6½ years. Check that your loan has no prepayment penalty and ask your servicer to apply extra payments to principal.

**What property tax rate should I use?**
Use the rate or yearly bill for the specific home: listings and county assessor websites show the current tax. Rates vary a lot between states and counties, and taxes are based on the assessed value, which can differ from the price.

### At a glance

### How to calculate a car payment

### Guide

#### How the amount financed is worked out

Sales tax is charged on the price – less the trade-in in states that allow it, and usually before a manufacturer rebate. Whether fees such as the documentation fee are taxed varies by state; the calculator taxes the price only.

- **Price − rebate** – what the car costs after incentives.
- **− trade-in equity** – the trade-in value minus what you owe on it; if you owe more, the difference is added instead.
- **− down payment** – cash you pay at signing.
- **+ sales tax and fees** – if you choose to finance them rather than pay them upfront.

#### Car payment by term

For $29,690 financed at 6.5% APR. Long terms lower the payment but more than double the interest, and leave you owing more than the car is worth for longer.

| Term | Monthly payment | Total interest |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 36 months | $909.97 | $3,069 |
| 48 months | $704.10 | $4,107 |
| 60 months | $580.92 | $5,165 |
| 72 months | $499.09 | $6,244 |
| 84 months | $440.88 | $7,344 |

### FAQ

**How do I calculate my car payment?**
Work out the amount financed – price, minus rebate, trade-in equity and down payment, plus any tax and fees you finance – then apply P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), where r is the APR ÷ 12 and n the number of months. $29,690 at 6.5% for 60 months is $580.92.

**Does a trade-in reduce sales tax?**
In most states, yes: you pay sales tax only on the price minus the trade-in. California, Hawaii, Virginia and Washington DC tax the full price, and Michigan caps the credit. Check your state’s rules and set the switch to match.

**What happens if I owe more than my trade-in is worth?**
That negative equity is usually added to the new loan, so you pay interest on it and start the new loan upside down. Paying it off in cash, waiting until you have equity, or choosing a cheaper car avoids the trap.

**Is 0% APR or cash back better?**
It depends on the rebate, your own rate and the term. Enter both offers in **Low APR or cash back?** – the one with the lower total cost wins. Large rebates often beat a low rate on shorter loans; low rates win on longer ones.

**What is the out-the-door price?**
The full amount to buy the car: price minus rebates, plus sales tax and fees. Negotiating on the out-the-door price stops add-ons and fees from creeping in after you agree a price.

## Interactive Periodic Table

Interactive periodic table of all 118 elements: properties, electron configurations, trend heat maps, states at any temperature, a quiz and a printable PDF.

### At a glance

### Features

- **Everything about an element**: Point at an element for a quick read-out; click it for the full card — configuration with a copy button, shells, Bohr model, oxidation states and physical properties in the units you choose.
- **See the trends**: Turn the table into a heat map of electronegativity, atomic radius, ionisation energy, electron affinity, melting point, boiling point, density or atomic weight, and plot the same property against atomic number.
- **Solid, liquid or gas**: Slide the temperature from absolute zero to the surface of the Sun and watch elements melt and boil. Carbon and arsenic sublime; helium never freezes at normal pressure.
- **Search that understands families**: Type “halogens”, “noble gases”, “group 2”, “period 4” or “f-block” to light up a whole family, or a name, symbol or number to jump to one element.
- **Learn it by heart**: Three quiz types and six ranges, from the first 20 elements to the full table. Hard mode hides every symbol so you find elements from their place alone.

### How to use the periodic table

1. **Find an element** — Click it in the table, or type its name, symbol or atomic number in the search box and press Enter.
2. **Read its properties** — The card under the table lists its configuration, shells, oxidation states, electronegativity, radius, energies, melting and boiling points and density. Use the arrows to step to the next element.
3. **Colour the table** — Pick **Colour by** — family, block, metals and nonmetals, state of matter, or a property heat map. Point at a legend entry to light up that group.
4. **Change the temperature** — In the state-of-matter view, drag the slider or pick a preset such as body temperature to see what melts and boils.
5. **Quiz yourself or print** — Choose **Quiz** to practise, or **Print & download** for a PDF, PNG or SVG of the table.

### Guide

#### How the periodic table is arranged

Elements are placed in order of **atomic number** — the number of protons — in 7 rows called **periods** and 18 columns called **groups**. Elements in the same group have the same arrangement of outer electrons, which is why they behave alike: the alkali metals in group 1 all react with water, the halogens in group 17 all form salts, the noble gases in group 18 hardly react at all.

The table splits into **blocks** named after the subshell being filled: the s-block (groups 1–2 and helium), the p-block (groups 13–18), the d-block (groups 3–12, the transition metals) and the f-block (the two rows shown underneath, which would make the table 32 columns wide if fitted in).

This table puts **lutetium and lawrencium in group 3**, under scandium and yttrium, and the 14 elements from lanthanum to ytterbium and from actinium to nobelium in the f-block rows — the layout an IUPAC project report favoured in 2021. Many textbooks, including NCERT’s, put lanthanum and actinium in group 3 instead; the elements and their properties are the same either way.

#### Periodic trends at a glance

Trends have exceptions — nitrogen’s ionisation energy is higher than oxygen’s, and fluorine’s electron affinity is lower than chlorine’s — so the heat maps and the trend chart are worth a look rather than relying on the rule alone.

| Property | Across a period (left → right) | Down a group | Highest |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Atomic radius | Decreases | Increases | Francium (348 pm, van der Waals) |
| Electronegativity | Increases | Decreases | Fluorine (3.98) |
| First ionisation energy | Increases | Decreases | Helium (24.587 eV) |
| Electron affinity | Generally increases | Generally decreases | Chlorine (3.617 eV) |
| Metallic character | Decreases | Increases | Caesium and francium |

#### Where the data come from

- Names and **atomic weights**: IUPAC and its Commission on Isotopic Abundances and Atomic Weights (CIAAW, 2021 abridged values).
- **Electron configurations**: built by the same engine as our [Electron Configuration Builder](https://justtools.online/education-tools/electron-configuration/), which is checked against the NIST Atomic Spectra Database.
- **Electronegativity, radius, ionisation energy, electron affinity, oxidation states, melting and boiling points, density and families**: PubChem’s periodic table (US National Library of Medicine), compiled from Jefferson Lab and Los Alamos National Laboratory. Three values are corrected: helium has no melting point at normal pressure, and carbon and arsenic sublime instead of melting.
- Astatine, francium and the elements from fermium (100) on have never been made in a visible amount, so their physical values are estimates; from meitnerium (109) on, even the chemistry is a prediction. The page says so wherever it shows them.

#### The first 20 elements

Many school syllabuses ask for the first 20 (or 30) elements by heart. In order: hydrogen (H), helium (He), lithium (Li), beryllium (Be), boron (B), carbon (C), nitrogen (N), oxygen (O), fluorine (F), neon (Ne), sodium (Na), magnesium (Mg), aluminium (Al), silicon (Si), phosphorus (P), sulfur (S), chlorine (Cl), argon (Ar), potassium (K) and calcium (Ca). Use the quiz with **First 20** to practise them until they stick.

### FAQ

**How many elements are in the periodic table?**
118. The last four — nihonium (113), moscovium (115), tennessine (117) and oganesson (118) — were named in 2016, completing the seventh period.

**Why are some atomic weights in square brackets?**
Those elements have no stable isotope, so they have no standard atomic weight. The number in brackets is the mass number of the longest-lived isotope, e.g. [97] for technetium.

**Which elements are liquid at room temperature?**
At 25 °C only **bromine** and **mercury**. Gallium (29.8 °C), caesium (28.4 °C) and rubidium (39.3 °C) melt just above it — set the state-of-matter slider to body temperature and gallium and caesium turn liquid.

**Where do the lanthanides and actinides go?**
In the two rows under the main table. They belong between groups 2 and 3 but would make the table 32 columns wide, so they are printed separately. This table puts lutetium and lawrencium in group 3; some books put lanthanum and actinium there.

**What do the colours mean?**
In the default view each colour is a family: alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, transition metals, post-transition metals, metalloids, nonmetals, halogens, noble gases, lanthanides and actinides. Point at a legend entry to light up its members. Other views colour by block, by metal type, by state or by the size of a property.

**Can I print the periodic table?**
Yes. Choose **Print & download**, pick the paper (A4, Letter, A3 or Tabloid), colour or black and white, and what each box shows — full details, symbols, numbers only or blank. Print it directly, or download a PDF, PNG or SVG. Keep the scale at 100% when printing the PDF.

**Is the electron configuration shown measured or predicted?**
For elements up to hassium (108) it matches NIST’s measured ground states, including exceptions such as chromium ([Ar] 3d⁵ 4s¹) and copper ([Ar] 3d¹⁰ 4s¹). Beyond that the configurations come from theory.

**Does it work offline?**
Yes. Everything — data, quiz and PDF — runs in your browser. Settings and quiz best scores are saved on your device only.

## CSS Flexbox & Grid Playground

Learn and build CSS flexbox and grid layouts visually: try every property, watch items move, draw grid areas, then copy CSS, HTML, Tailwind or React code.

### At a glance

- Covers **every flexbox container property** (flex-direction, flex-wrap, justify-content, align-items, align-content, gap) and **every flex item property** (flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, align-self, order).

- **See what each property does**: Every value is a button, and the preview updates as you click. A sentence under each property explains the current value — no need to keep a cheat sheet open.
- **Main axis, cross axis, made visible**: The preview names the main and cross axes for the current flex-direction, so justify-content and align-items finally make sense when you switch to column.
- **Real sizes on every item**: Change flex-grow, flex-shrink or flex-basis and watch each item’s width in pixels. Narrow the container to see shrinking and wrapping happen.
- **Grid lines you can draw on**: Numbered grid lines sit over the layout. Turn on drawing and drag across cells to give an item its column and row lines.

### How to build a layout with flexbox or grid

1. **Pick Flexbox or Grid** — Flexbox lays items out in one direction (a row or a column); grid places them in rows and columns at once. Or start from one of the examples.
2. **Set the container** — Click values such as justify-content: space-between or grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) and watch the preview.
3. **Adjust single items** — Click an item, then give it flex-grow, a fixed flex-basis, its own alignment, or grid lines and spans. In grid mode you can drag its area on the grid.
4. **Test it** — Drag the container width slider to see how the layout responds on narrow screens.
5. **Copy the code** — Choose CSS, HTML, Tailwind or React, then Copy or Download. Share builds a link to this exact layout.

### Guide

#### Flexbox or grid?

**Flexbox** is for laying things out along one line — a navigation bar, a row of buttons, a card’s header and footer — where the content decides the sizes and items may wrap. **Grid** is for two-dimensional layouts — page structure, galleries, dashboards — where you define the columns and rows first and place items into them.

They work well together: a grid for the page, flexbox inside each card.

#### The properties people mix up

In flexbox, switching flex-direction to column swaps the axes: justify-content then works vertically and align-items horizontally. justify-items does nothing in flexbox.

| Property | Works along | What it moves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| justify-content | Main axis (flex) / inline axis (grid) | The items as a group (flex) or the whole set of tracks (grid) |
| align-items | Cross axis (flex) / block axis (grid) | Each item inside its line or grid area |
| align-content | Cross axis | Whole lines of wrapped items (flex) or rows of tracks (grid) |
| justify-items | Inline axis (grid only) | Each item inside its grid area |
| align-self / justify-self | Same as align-items / justify-items | One item, overriding the container |

#### flex-grow, flex-shrink and flex-basis

- **flex-basis** is the starting size along the main axis. `auto` uses the item’s width (or its content); `0` ignores content so space is shared purely by flex-grow.
- **flex-grow** shares out leftover space: an item with 2 gets twice as much of the extra as an item with 1. With 0 it never grows.
- **flex-shrink** decides who gives up space when there is not enough; 0 means the item never shrinks below its basis.
- The shorthand `flex: 1` means `1 1 0%`; `flex: auto` means `1 1 auto`; `flex: none` means `0 0 auto`. This tool always writes all three values so nothing is hidden.

#### auto-fill vs auto-fit

`repeat(auto-fill, minmax(140px, 1fr))` makes as many 140px-or-wider columns as fit, keeping empty columns when there are few items. `auto-fit` does the same but collapses empty columns, so a few items stretch across the full width. Load the **Responsive cards** example, remove items and switch between the two to see the difference.

### FAQ

**What is the difference between justify-content and align-items?**
justify-content distributes items along the main axis (left to right in a row); align-items positions them on the cross axis (top to bottom in a row). Switch flex-direction to column and they swap directions.

**Why does align-content do nothing?**
In flexbox it only affects containers whose items wrap onto more than one line — set flex-wrap: wrap and give the container some height. In grid it moves the rows when they are shorter than the container.

**Why does my flex item not shrink below its text?**
Flex items have a default min-width of auto, so they will not shrink below their longest word or a fixed-size child. Add min-width: 0 to the item (min-w-0 in Tailwind) to let it shrink.

**What does 1fr mean in CSS grid?**
One fraction of the leftover space. In grid-template-columns: 1fr 2fr, the second column gets twice the free space of the first. Note that 1fr has a minimum of auto, so long content can widen it; minmax(0, 1fr) — what Tailwind’s grid-cols-3 uses — prevents that.

**Is the Tailwind code for Tailwind v3 or v4?**
Tailwind CSS v4. Most classes are the same in v3, but v4 accepts any spacing step (gap-13, basis-30); in v3 use an arbitrary value such as gap-[52px] for steps the default scale lacks.

**Can I use gap with flexbox?**
Yes — in Chrome 84+, Edge 84+, Firefox 63+ and Safari 14.1+. For much older browsers use margins on the items instead.

**Does order change the reading order?**
No. order, row-reverse, column-reverse and grid placement change only what you see. Screen readers and keyboard focus follow the HTML, so the tool warns you when the two may differ.

**Is my layout saved?**
Yes, in your browser on this device. Use Share to copy a link that opens the same layout anywhere — it is stored in the link itself, not on a server.

| A6 pass | 148 × 105 | 5.8 × 4.1 | Large event, backstage or vehicle passes |

#### Printing on paper

- Print at **100% / Actual size**. “Fit to page” shrinks the cards slightly, so they no longer fit standard holders.
- For double-sided cards, print the front sheet, then the back sheet on the other side. Most printers flip on the **long edge**; if your backs come out upside down, choose “flip on short edge” instead.
- Thick paper or card stock (250–300 gsm) gives the best result; then laminate the cards and cut along the marks.
- Do a test on plain paper first and hold it up to the light to check that fronts and backs line up.

#### Printing on PVC cards

Direct-to-card PVC printers print through a printer driver set to the card size. Choose **Card printer (one per page)**: the PDF then has one card-sized page per side — front, back, next front — which the driver prints in order (set it to double-sided for backs).

Card printers cannot print right to the edge on every model; keep important text a few millimetres in from the border, as the layouts here already do.

#### Bulk cards from a spreadsheet

Put one person per row with a heading row on top: **Name**, the line under the name (Designation, Class…), each field label and **Photo**. Download the sample CSV to see the exact headings for your template. Headings such as Dept, DOB, Mobile or Blood are understood too.

Name each photo after the person’s card number (EMP-1042.jpg) or name (Priya Sharma.jpg), or type its file name in the Photo column, then add all the photos at once.

### FAQ

**What size is a standard ID card?**
85.6 × 54 mm (3.375 × 2.125 in) — the ISO/IEC 7810 ID-1 size, also called CR80, the same as a credit card. It has rounded corners of about 3.2 mm.

**How many ID cards fit on an A4 sheet?**
Ten landscape cards (2 × 5) or nine portrait cards (3 × 3), leaving a 6 mm margin that most printers need. US Letter takes eight landscape or nine portrait cards.

**Can I make ID cards for a whole class or company at once?**
Yes. Paste rows from Excel or Google Sheets, or open a CSV, and add the photos. Up to 500 people go into one print PDF.

**What can the QR code contain?**
The card number, a link or text with placeholders such as https://example.com/verify/{id}, or a vCard contact with name, organisation, title, phone and website. A barcode (Code 128) can hold the card number or short text.

**Will it work with my PVC card printer?**
Choose “Card printer (one per page)”: every page is exactly card size, which is what card printer drivers expect. Print a single test card first to check alignment.

**Are the photos and details uploaded anywhere?**
No. The cards are made in your browser. The design and the single card you edit are saved on this device so they are there next time; imported lists and photos are kept only while the tab is open.

**Can I put a signature on the card?**
Yes, on the back: upload a photo of the signature (on white paper, cropped close) and set the signatory’s title.

**Does it support Hindi names?**
Yes — names and fields in Devanagari are drawn with a font that covers it, with the vowel signs in the right places.

### At a glance

- Checks every invoice against **article 63 §8 of the Luxembourg VAT law** (loi modifiée du 12 février 1979, AED coordinated text of 1 January 2026): number in an unbroken series, dates, both parties’ names and addresses, VAT numbers, description, unit prices, the base and VAT per rate.

- For the **small-business franchise** (turnover up to €50,000 a year since 1 January 2025) it prints the AED’s own wording — “TVA non applicable – Article 57bis de la loi modifiée du 12 février 1979” — and leaves VAT off the invoice.

- Adds a **SEPA payment QR code** (EPC069-12) with an ISO 11649 RF reference, and exports a **Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 e-invoice (UBL)** that passes the official EN 16931 and Peppol validation rules.

### Features

- **A checklist, not just a template**: As you type, the tool lists anything article 63 of the VAT law or the company law still needs — a missing customer VAT number for reverse charge, an RCS number, an exemption reference — before you send the invoice.
- **The right VAT treatment**: Tell it where the customer is and whether you sell goods or services: it suggests Luxembourg VAT, reverse charge, intra-EU exemption, export or out-of-scope, and prints the matching legal wording.
- **Three languages**: French, German and English — the languages of business in Luxembourg — or two at once, with dates and amounts written the local way.
- **Get paid faster**: Your IBAN and BIC are checked, and a SEPA QR code lets customers pay from banking apps that read EPC QR codes, with a structured RF reference.
- **Ready for e-invoicing**: Download a Peppol BIS 3.0 UBL file for public-sector customers, validated against the official rules — the same format Luxembourg plans for business invoices.

### How to make a Luxembourg invoice

1. **Enter your business** — Name, legal form, address, VAT number (LU…), RCS number and bank details. They are saved for next time.
2. **Add the customer** — Name, address, country and — for a business — their VAT number. Pick business or private person.
3. **Choose the VAT treatment** — Luxembourg VAT, small-business franchise, EU business (services or goods), export, services outside the EU or exempt. The tool suggests the usual one.
4. **Add the lines** — Description, quantity, unit, unit price excluding VAT, any discount and the VAT rate (17, 14, 8 or 3 %).
5. **Check and download** — Fix anything the checklist flags, choose the language, then download the PDF — or the Peppol e-invoice for public bodies.

### Guide

#### What a Luxembourg invoice must show

Article 63 §8 of the VAT law lists the details; the company law of 10 August 1915 adds the identification of companies. This tool prints all of them:

- The **date of issue** and a **unique sequential number**, which may follow one or more series.
- Your **VAT number**, and the **customer’s VAT number** when they account for the VAT (reverse charge) or receive an intra-Community supply of goods.
- The **full name and address** of both parties.
- The **quantity and nature** of the goods or the **extent and nature** of the services, and the **date of supply** if it differs from the invoice date.
- The **taxable amount for each rate** or exemption, the **unit price excluding VAT**, discounts, the **rate** and the **VAT due**.
- For an exemption, the **legal reference**; for reverse charge, **“Autoliquidation”**; with cash accounting, **“Comptabilité de caisse”**.
- For a company: its name with the **legal form** (SA, SARL…), the **registered office** and **“R.C.S. Luxembourg”** with its registration number.

#### Luxembourg VAT rates

Which rate applies depends on the annexes of the VAT law and its regulations — check with the AED (Administration de l’enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA) if you are not sure for a given product.

| Rate | Name | Typical uses |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 17 % | Normal rate | Most goods and services |
| 14 % | Intermediate rate | Wines up to 13 % alcohol, mineral fuels and heating oil, washing and cleaning products, advertising print, custody of securities (annex C) |
| 8 % | Reduced rate | Gas, electricity, district heating, firewood, hairdressing, repairs of shoes, clothes and household appliances, bicycles (annex A) |
| 3 % | Super-reduced rate | Food (not alcoholic drinks), books and newspapers, children’s clothes, medicines, restaurant meals (not alcohol), hotels, passenger transport, entry to culture and sport (annex B) |

#### Small businesses: the VAT franchise

Businesses established in Luxembourg whose annual turnover in Luxembourg does not exceed **€50,000** (the threshold since 1 January 2025) can use the franchise: they charge no VAT and cannot deduct it. If turnover passes €50,000 the exemption continues until the end of the year as long as it stays within €55,000; above that it ends the next day (AED SME scheme FAQ).

Franchise invoices may not show VAT and must carry the statement “TVA non applicable – Article 57bis de la loi modifiée du 12 février 1979”. Since 2025 they may also be simplified invoices.

#### E-invoicing in Luxembourg

Invoices to Luxembourg **public bodies** must be electronic, in the European standard EN 16931 sent over Peppol — for all suppliers since 18 March 2023. The **e-invoice (UBL)** button makes such a file; send it through a Peppol access point or the State’s e-invoicing service.

For **business-to-business** invoices, a government bill (n° 8815, filed in July 2026) proposes compulsory e-invoicing from 2028 for receiving and from 2028–2029 for issuing. It is still a draft; until it becomes law, PDF invoices remain fine between businesses.

### FAQ

**Do I have to write my invoice in French?**
No. Invoices can be in any language, but the AED may ask for a French or German translation of invoices in another language (art. 63 §12). French, German and English — or bilingual — are built in.

**When must an invoice be issued?**
At the latest on the 15th day of the month after the month of the supply, and for an advance payment at the latest when you receive it (art. 63 §5). The checklist warns you when the invoice date is later.

**What do I write for a customer in another EU country?**
For services to a business, no Luxembourg VAT is charged and the invoice says “Autoliquidation” (reverse charge), with the customer’s VAT number. For goods shipped to a VAT-registered business in another EU country, the supply is exempt (art. 43 §1 d) and the invoice says so. Choose the matching regime and the wording is added.

**I am a freelancer under the franchise. What goes on my invoice?**
No VAT, and the statement “TVA non applicable – Article 57bis de la loi modifiée du 12 février 1979”. Switch on “I use the VAT franchise” and the tool does the rest.

**Is an RCS number required on invoices?**
For commercial companies, yes: the 1915 company law requires the name, legal form, registered office and “R.C.S. Luxembourg” followed by the registration number on invoices and letters.

**What is a simplified invoice?**
An invoice with fewer details, allowed when the total including VAT is no more than €100, for documents that amend an earlier invoice, and for businesses under the franchise (art. 63 §10–11). This tool always produces a full invoice, which is valid in every case.

**Does the SEPA QR code work with my bank?**
It follows the European Payments Council standard (EPC069-12, also called GiroCode). Many banking apps in the euro area can read it; if a customer’s app cannot, the IBAN and reference are printed beside it.

**Is my data uploaded?**
No. The invoice is built in your browser. Your business details, logo and customers are saved on this device only, so they are there next time.

## Connect Four

URL: https://justtools.online/games/connect-four/
Category: Games
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-20

Play Connect Four online free: drop discs and get four in a row against the computer — Easy, Medium or Hard — or a friend on one device. No sign-up.

### At a glance

- The classic **7-column, 6-row** board, plus larger **8×7** and **9×7** boards for a longer game.
- Play the computer on **Easy, Medium or Hard**, or a friend taking turns on the same phone, tablet or computer.
- Hard searches many moves ahead — with alpha-beta pruning and a transposition table — for up to a second per move and never misses a win or a block it can see.
- Connect Four is a **solved game**: with perfect play the first player wins by starting in the centre column, at the latest on the 41st move. James D. Allen and Victor Allis proved it independently in October 1988.
- The 7×6 board has **4,531,985,219,092** possible positions.
- Hints, undo, sound, full screen and keyboard play (keys 1–7 drop a disc); scores are kept on your device. Free, with no download or sign-up.

### Features

- **An opponent for everyone**: Easy for children, Medium for a fair game and Hard for a real challenge — it blocks threats and sets up its own.
- **Two players, one screen**: Pass the phone or share the keyboard, with your own names and a running score.
- **Learn the tricks**: Ask for a hint to see the strongest column — it tells you when a forced win is on the board.
- **Fair starts**: Turn on “Take turns going first” so the first move swaps every game — going first is a real advantage.
- **Bigger boards**: Try 8×7 or 9×7 for more room to build threats.
- **Plays anywhere**: Phones, tablets and computers, with keyboard control and screen-reader announcements of every move.

### How to play Connect Four

1. **Pick an opponent** — Choose **Computer** and a difficulty, and your colour — Red moves first — or **A friend** to play on the same device.
2. **Drop a disc** — Tap a column (or press its number). The disc falls to the lowest free space.
3. **Make four in a row** — Line up four of your discs across, down or diagonally before your opponent does. A full board with no line is a draw.
4. **Play again** — Press **Play again** — the score keeps adding up. Use **Hint** or **Undo** while you learn.

### Guide

#### Connect Four strategy

- **Take the centre.** The middle column is part of more possible lines than any other — that is why perfect play starts there.
- **Block threes at once.** If your opponent has three in a row with an empty square they can reach, drop there before anything else.
- **Build double threats.** Two winning squares at the same time can’t both be blocked — the most common way games are won.
- **Watch the square below.** Don’t fill the space directly under your opponent’s winning square: your disc lets theirs land on it.
- **Think in rows.** The first player usually wants threats on odd rows (counting from the bottom), the second player on even rows — a key idea in Victor Allis’s solution.

#### How the computer plays

The computer reads the board column by column, tries the centre first and looks ahead with a minimax search pruned by alpha-beta, remembering positions it has already scored. When it can’t see to the end of the game it scores the board by the open lines each side still has. Hard thinks for up to a second and often looks ten or more moves ahead; it is strong, but it is not a perfect solver — a well-built trap can still beat it.

### FAQ

**Who wins Connect Four with perfect play?**
The first player. Starting in the middle column, the first player can always force a win — at the latest on the 41st move. James D. Allen and Victor Allis showed this independently in 1988.

**How many positions are there in Connect Four?**
On the standard 7×6 board there are 4,531,985,219,092 legal positions.

**Can I play against a friend?**
Yes — choose **A friend** and take turns on the same device. You can type your names, and the score is kept for each board size.

**Is the Hard level unbeatable?**
No, but it is tough: it never misses a win or a block it can see and looks many moves ahead. Set up two threats at once, or a threat it can’t reach in time, to beat it.

**Can I take back a move?**
Yes. **Undo** takes back your last move (and the computer’s reply). Use **Hint** to see the column the computer would pick for you.

**Does it work offline?**
Once the page has loaded, yes — the game and the computer run entirely in your browser, and nothing is sent anywhere.

## Reversi

URL: https://justtools.online/games/reversi/
Category: Games
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-20

Play Reversi online free — the disc-flipping strategy game — against the computer (Easy, Medium, Hard) or a friend. 6×6, 8×8 or 10×10 boards. No sign-up.

### At a glance

- Standard rules on the **8×8** board — Black moves first from the four centre discs — plus **6×6** and **10×10** boards.
- Play the computer on **Easy, Medium or Hard**, or a friend on the same device; possible moves are marked, and pointing at one shows which discs would turn.
- Hard searches ahead for about a second per move, values corners, edges and mobility, and plays the **last 12 moves of an 8×8 game perfectly** with an exact endgame search.
- The computer’s solver was checked on the 4×4 board, where perfect play is known: **White wins 11–3**.
- Small boards are solved: on **6×6, White wins 16–20** with perfect play. For 8×8, a 2023 computer study (a preprint by Hiroki Takizawa) reports that perfect play leads to a draw.
- Hints, undo, the full move list in standard notation (f5 d6 …), sound, full screen and keyboard play. Free, with no sign-up.

### Features

- **Three levels**: Easy to learn the rules, Medium for a fair game, Hard for a real fight — it knows the value of corners.
- **See every move**: Dots mark the squares you can play; point at one to see exactly which discs it turns.
- **Passes handled for you**: When a player has no move the turn passes automatically, and the game ends when neither side can move.
- **Learn from hints**: Hint shows the computer’s choice; near the end it tells you the final margin with perfect play.
- **Two players, one screen**: Play a friend with your own names and a running score for each board size.
- **Notation**: Every game is recorded in standard notation, a1 at the top-left — paste it into any Reversi program to study.

### How to play Reversi

1. **Choose an opponent** — Pick **Computer** and a difficulty, and Black (moves first) or White — or **A friend**.
2. **Outflank** — Place a disc so that one or more straight lines of your opponent’s discs lie between it and another of your discs — across, down or diagonally. Those discs turn to your colour.
3. **Pass if you must** — If you have no square that outflanks anything, your turn passes. If you can move, you must.
4. **Count the discs** — When neither player can move, the one with more discs on the board wins.

### Guide

#### Reversi strategy

- **Corners can never be flipped.** Take them when you can — and avoid the squares next to an empty corner (b2, g2, b7, g7 and the edge squares beside the corners), which tend to give it away.
- **Fewer discs early is often better.** Having many discs in the opening limits your own moves; keep your options (mobility) and squeeze your opponent’s.
- **Edges are strong but not always safe.** A lone edge disc can be outflanked along the edge.
- **Parity in the endgame.** Try to make the last move in each region of empty squares.

#### Reversi or Othello?

Reversi is the original name of the game, from the 1880s. The modern version — with the four centre discs placed in a fixed cross pattern and Black moving first — is sold under the trademark Othello, and those are the rules used here. JustTools is not connected with the Othello trademark owners.

### FAQ

**Who moves first in Reversi?**
Black. The game starts with two black and two white discs crossed in the centre (d5 and e4 black, d4 and e5 white), and Black has four possible first moves: d3, c4, f5 and e6.

**What happens if I can’t move?**
You pass and your opponent moves again. If neither player can move, the game ends and the discs are counted.

**Is Reversi solved?**
The 4×4 and 6×6 boards are: White wins both with perfect play (6×6 ends 16–20). For the standard 8×8 board, a 2023 preprint by Hiroki Takizawa reports a computer proof that perfect play is a draw.

**How strong is the Hard computer?**
It looks several moves ahead with alpha-beta search, values corners, edges and mobility, and plays the last 12 moves on 8×8 perfectly. Strong club players can still beat it in the middle game.

**Can I play against a friend?**
Yes — choose **A friend** and take turns on the same device.

**Is my game saved?**
Your settings and scores are kept in your browser on this device. Nothing is sent to a server.

## Checkers

URL: https://justtools.online/games/checkers/
Category: Games
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-20

Play checkers online free against the computer or a friend: American/English checkers plus international, Brazilian and Russian draughts. No sign-up.

### At a glance

- Four rule sets: **American / English checkers** (8×8), **international draughts** (10×10), **Brazilian draughts** (8×8) and **Russian draughts (shashki)** (8×8).
- Every rule that differs between them is built in: backward captures by men, **flying kings**, the rule to **capture the most pieces** (international and Brazilian), and the Russian rule that a man crowned mid-jump keeps jumping as a king.
- Captures are compulsory and multi-jumps must be finished; jumped pieces leave the board only when the move ends, so no piece can be jumped twice.
- Play the computer on **Easy, Medium or Hard** — Hard thinks for about a second a move and follows every exchange to its end — or a friend on one device.
- English checkers is **solved**: Jonathan Schaeffer’s team showed in 2007 (Science) that perfect play from the start is a draw. The game has 500,995,484,682,338,672,639 possible positions.
- Hints, undo, a move list in standard notation (11-15 or e3-d4), optional square numbers, sound and keyboard play. Free, with no sign-up.

### Features

- **The rules you grew up with**: Pick American checkers, international draughts, Brazilian or Russian rules — the board, first player and capture rules follow automatically.
- **Captures made clear**: When a jump is compulsory the tool says so and rings the pieces that must jump; landing squares are marked for the piece you pick.
- **Multi-jumps your way**: Click each landing square in turn, or go straight to the final square when only one route ends there.
- **A computer that fights back**: Three levels, from random-ish moves for beginners to a search that sees exchanges coming.
- **Learn the notation**: Moves are written the standard way for each variant, with optional square numbers on the board.
- **Two players, one screen**: Play a friend with your own names; the board turns so the first player sits at the bottom.

### How to play checkers

1. **Choose the rules** — American / English checkers is the default; pick international, Brazilian or Russian draughts if that is what you play.
2. **Choose an opponent** — Play the **Computer** at Easy, Medium or Hard (and choose your colour), or **A friend** on the same device.
3. **Move diagonally** — Click one of your pieces, then a highlighted square. Men move forward one square on the dark squares; kings move both ways.
4. **Capture by jumping** — Jump over an opponent’s piece to an empty square beyond it. If you can capture, you must — and keep jumping while you can.
5. **Crown and win** — A man reaching the far row becomes a king. You win when your opponent has no pieces left or no legal move.

### Guide

#### How the rule sets differ

|  | American / English | International | Brazilian | Russian |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Board | 8×8 | 10×10 | 8×8 | 8×8 |
| Pieces each | 12 | 20 | 12 | 12 |
| Moves first | Dark | Light | Light | Light |
| Men capture backwards | No | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Kings | One square | Flying (any distance) | Flying | Flying |
| Must take the most pieces | No | Yes | Yes | No |
| Man reaching the far row mid-jump | Is crowned; move ends | Not crowned unless it ends there | Not crowned unless it ends there | Is crowned and keeps jumping |

#### Checkers strategy

- **Control the centre.** Pieces in the middle of the board have more moves and support each other.
- **Keep your back row.** Leaving your own back-row pieces at home stops the opponent from crowning cheaply.
- **Use the compulsory capture.** Offer a piece so that the forced jump lands your opponent where you can take two back.
- **Trade when ahead.** With a piece more, swapping pieces off makes your advantage count.
- **Kings win endgames.** Get a king early in the endgame — in the flying-king variants one king can control whole diagonals.

#### When the game is a draw

In every variant a game is drawn when the same position, with the same player to move, comes up a third time. Each rule set also ends games that make no progress after a set number of moves by each side, and the tool applies these automatically, warning you in the last ten moves. A player who cannot move loses, whether their pieces are all gone or just blocked.

| Rules | Automatic draw after |
| --- | --- |
| American / English | 40 moves each without a capture or a man moving. Official rules have no automatic limit: a player who refuses a draw offer must show a win within 40 moves. With no draw offers here, the limit applies to every game. |
| International (FMJD) | 25 moves each with only kings moving and no captures; 16 moves each with three pieces (at least one a king) against a lone king; 5 moves each with two pieces or one, including a king, against a lone king. |
| Brazilian | 20 moves each with only kings moving and no captures, which also covers three kings against one. |
| Russian | 15 moves each with only kings moving and no captures, or with three or more kings against a lone king; with kings on both sides and no capture or crowning, 5 moves in 2–3 piece endings, 30 in 4–5 and 60 in 6–7; 5 moves with three pieces against a lone king on the main road (a1–h8). |

### FAQ

**Is capturing compulsory in checkers?**
Yes, in all four rule sets: if you can jump, you must, and a multi-jump must be finished. In American checkers and Russian draughts you may choose which capture to make; in international and Brazilian draughts you must take the greatest number of pieces.

**Who moves first in checkers?**
In American / English checkers the dark pieces (often red or black) move first. In international, Brazilian and Russian draughts, light (white) moves first.

**Can kings move more than one square?**
In American checkers, no — a king moves one square diagonally in any direction. In international, Brazilian and Russian draughts kings “fly”: they move any distance along a diagonal and can capture from afar.

**Is checkers solved?**
Yes. In 2007 Jonathan Schaeffer’s team at the University of Alberta published a proof (in Science) that English checkers is a draw with perfect play from the starting position.

**How do I make a multiple jump?**
Click the piece, then click each landing square in turn — or click the final square directly if only one route ends there. The tool won’t let you stop part-way.

**When is a game of checkers a draw?**
When the same position comes up three times with the same player to move, or when nobody makes progress for a set number of moves: 40 moves each without a capture or a man moving in American checkers, 25 moves of kings only in international draughts, 20 in Brazilian and 15 in Russian draughts. Endgames against a lone king have shorter limits in international and Russian rules.

**Can I play against a friend?**
Yes — choose **A friend** and take turns on the same device. The board shows the player who moves first at the bottom.

### How to play Snake

1. **Start moving** — Press an arrow key, swipe on the board or tap **Play**. The snake keeps moving forward on its own.
2. **Steer to the apple** — Turn up, down, left or right to reach the red apple. Each apple makes the snake one square longer and is worth 10 points.
3. **Grab golden apples** — After every fifth apple a golden one appears for a short time. The faster you reach it, the more points it gives — up to 50.
4. **Don’t crash** — Hitting a wall, an obstacle or your own body ends the game. With **Wrap around** on, the edges take you to the other side instead.
5. **Fill the board** — Keep going until the snake fills every free square — the perfect game.

### Guide

#### Scoring

|  | Points | Snake grows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Apple | 10 | One square |
| Golden apple | 10–50, more the sooner you reach it | No |
| Every free square filled | You win | — |

#### Tips for a higher score

- **Hug the edges early.** Running along the walls keeps the middle of the board open for later.
- **Don’t chase every apple directly.** When the snake is long, a short cut can wall you in; take the long way round if it keeps a path back to your tail.
- **Follow your tail when in doubt.** The square your tail is leaving is always safe to move into next.
- **Plan your turns early.** You can press two or three turns ahead and they will be played one square at a time.
- **Start slow, then speed up.** Learn a board size at Slow or Normal before trying Fast or Insane.

#### A short history of Snake

The idea began with **Blockade** (1976), a two-player arcade game from Gremlin Industries in which each player leaves a growing wall behind them and tries to outlast the other. The first known home-computer version, *Worm*, appeared for the TRS-80 in 1978, and single-player games where the snake eats items and grows — such as *Snake Byte* and the arcade game *Nibbler*, both 1982 — followed.

Many PC users first met it as *Nibbles*, a sample program that came with QBasic on MS-DOS from 1991. Then in 1998 Nokia put **Snake**, written by Taneli Armanto, on the Nokia 6110 and 5110 phones. It became one of the best-known mobile games ever: Nokia says 350 million copies exist, and in 2012 New York’s Museum of Modern Art named it among the video games it wanted for its collection.

### FAQ

**How do you play Snake?**
Steer the snake with the arrow keys (or W A S D, or by swiping on a phone) to eat the apples. Each apple makes it longer. The game ends if the snake hits a wall, an obstacle or its own body.

**Can you win at Snake?**
Yes — if the snake fills every free square on the board, you win. It is very hard on a large board, so try a small board first.

**What does wrap-around mean?**
With **Wrap around** on, leaving one edge of the board brings the snake back in on the opposite side, so only obstacles and your own body can end the game. With **Solid walls**, the edges are deadly.

**How do I play Snake on my phone?**
Swipe on the board in the direction you want to go — you can keep your finger down and swipe again to turn twice. Or switch on **On-screen arrows** for large buttons below the board.

**Does the computer’s game count towards my best score?**
No. If you press **Computer plays** at any point in a game, that game isn’t added to your records. Press an arrow key at any time to take over.

**Why did the game pause?**
It pauses by itself when you switch to another tab or window, or scroll the board off the screen, so you never lose a game by accident. Press Space or tap the board to carry on.

**What was the first Snake game?**
The genre began with Blockade, a two-player arcade game released by Gremlin Industries in 1976. Nokia’s Snake, which made the game famous on phones, followed in 1998.

## Solitaire
