#### How a pahada is recited

In Hindi, tables are learnt by chanting them. Each multiplier has its own word: **एकम** (×1), **दूनी** (×2), **तिया** (×3), **चौके** (×4), **पंजे** (×5), **छक्के** (×6), **सत्ते** (×7), **अट्ठे** (×8), **नवा** (×9) and **दहाई** (×10). So the table of 2 goes दो एकम दो, दो दूनी चार, दो तिया छह, दो चौके आठ, दो पंजे दस … दो दहाई बीस. Some regions use slightly different words, such as नम्मा for ×9. Beyond ×10 the tool reads it plainly: दो गुणा ग्यारह बराबर बाईस.

#### Tricks that make tables easier

| Table | Trick |
| --- | --- |
| 2 | Double the number. |
| 4 | Double it, then double again. |
| 5 | Answers end in 5 or 0 — half the number times 10. |
| 9 | The tens go up and the ones go down: 09, 18, 27, 36 … The digits add up to 9. |
| 10 | Put a 0 on the end. |
| 11 | Up to 9, repeat the digit: 11 × 6 = 66. |
| 12 | Times 10, plus double: 12 × 7 = 70 + 14 = 84. |
| Any | Swap the order: 8 × 3 is the same as 3 × 8, so every table you know helps with the others. |

### FAQ

**What is the table of 2?**
2 × 1 = 2, 2 × 2 = 4, 2 × 3 = 6, 2 × 4 = 8, 2 × 5 = 10, 2 × 6 = 12, 2 × 7 = 14, 2 × 8 = 16, 2 × 9 = 18, 2 × 10 = 20. In Hindi: दो एकम दो, दो दूनी चार … दो दहाई बीस.

**Can I see tables from 1 to 20 together?**
Yes. Open **All tables** and choose 1–20 (or any range up to 100). You can print them all on one page.

**How do I print a multiplication table?**
Press **Print** on a single table, a set of tables or the chart. Turn on **Hide answers** first to print a blank practice sheet.

**Can it read the table aloud in Hindi?**
Yes, if your device has a Hindi voice (most Android phones and Windows and Apple devices do). Otherwise it reads in English.

**How does the practice quiz choose questions?**
It picks from the tables you select, and every fact you miss gets more weight, so it comes back sooner. Facts you keep getting right are asked a little less. Your progress is saved in this browser only.

**What is the best way for a child to learn tables?**
Start with 2, 5 and 10, then 3, 4 and 11, and leave 6, 7, 8 and 9 for last. Practise a little every day, say the answers aloud, and use the fact that 3 × 8 = 8 × 3 — once 2 to 5 are learnt, half of the 6–9 tables are already known.

## Compound Interest Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/compound-interest-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-22

Free compound interest calculator: daily, monthly, quarterly or yearly compounding, regular deposits, the formula worked out, a growth chart and schedule.

### At a glance

- Compounds **yearly, half-yearly, quarterly, monthly, weekly, daily or continuously** — and compares all of them side by side for your numbers.
- Add **regular deposits** monthly, quarterly or yearly, at the start or end of each period, and raise them every year.
- Works backwards too: find the **starting amount**, **interest rate** or **time** needed to reach a target.
- Shows the **formula worked out** with your numbers — A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) — handy for homework and exams.
- Gives the **effective yearly rate** (APY), how long your money takes to **double**, and how much more you earn than with **simple interest**.
- A year-by-year chart and a monthly or yearly **schedule** you can download as CSV. Rupees, dollars, euros, pounds and dirhams.

### Features

- **Every compounding**: Yearly to daily, plus continuous compounding.
- **Regular deposits**: Monthly to yearly, start or end, with a yearly increase.
- **Solve for anything**: Final amount, starting amount, rate or time.
- **Formula shown**: Your values substituted into the formula.
- **Compare frequencies**: See what daily vs quarterly compounding is worth.
- **Chart and schedule**: Year by year or month by month, with CSV download.

### How to calculate compound interest

1. **Enter the starting amount** — The money you invest or deposit today (the principal).
2. **Set the rate and time** — The yearly interest rate and how many years (and months) it stays invested.
3. **Choose the compounding** — How often interest is added — quarterly for most Indian FDs, monthly or daily for many savings accounts.
4. **Add deposits if you like** — Turn on regular deposits to add money every month, quarter or year.
5. **Read the result** — The final amount, interest earned, effective rate, chart and schedule update as you type.

### Guide

#### The compound interest formula

**A = P × (1 + r/n)^(n × t)**, where **A** is the final amount, **P** the principal, **r** the yearly rate as a decimal (8% = 0.08), **n** the number of times interest is compounded each year and **t** the time in years. The interest earned is **A − P**. For continuous compounding the formula becomes **A = P × e^(r × t)**.

Example: ₹1,00,000 at 8% compounded quarterly for 5 years gives 1,00,000 × (1 + 0.08/4)^(4 × 5) = 1,00,000 × 1.02^20 = **₹1,48,594.74**, so the interest is ₹48,594.74. With simple interest it would be only ₹40,000.

#### How much does the compounding frequency matter?

| Compounding | ₹1 lakh at 8% for 10 years | Effective rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Yearly | ₹2,15,892 | 8.000% |
| Half-yearly | ₹2,19,112 | 8.160% |
| Quarterly | ₹2,20,804 | 8.243% |
| Monthly | ₹2,21,964 | 8.300% |
| Daily | ₹2,22,535 | 8.328% |
| Continuously | ₹2,22,554 | 8.329% |

#### The rule of 72

Divide 72 by the yearly interest rate to estimate how many years it takes money to double: at 8% that is about 9 years, at 12% about 6 years. The calculator shows both this quick estimate and the exact doubling time for your compounding.

### FAQ

**What is compound interest?**
Interest earned on both your original money and the interest already added to it. Because the interest itself earns interest, the balance grows faster every year — unlike simple interest, which is paid only on the original amount.

**How do I calculate compound interest?**
Use A = P(1 + r/n)^(nt) and subtract P. For ₹50,000 at 7% compounded yearly for 3 years: 50,000 × 1.07³ = ₹61,252.15, so the interest is ₹11,252.15. The calculator shows these steps with your own numbers.

**Is daily compounding better than monthly?**
Yes, slightly. At 8%, daily compounding gives an effective rate of 8.328% against 8.300% for monthly — on ₹1 lakh over 10 years that is about ₹570 more. See the comparison table for your numbers.

**How is an Indian bank FD compounded?**
Most banks compound fixed deposit interest quarterly. For a detailed FD calculation with senior-citizen rates and TDS, use the FD calculator.

**Can I find the rate I need to reach a target?**
Yes. Choose **Interest rate** under Calculate, enter the amount you want, the starting amount and the time, and the calculator finds the yearly rate needed. It can also find the time or the starting amount.

**What is the effective annual rate (APY)?**
The rate you really earn in a year once compounding is counted. 12% compounded monthly is 12.68% a year effectively. It lets you compare offers with different compounding.

## Date Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/date-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-22

Count the days between two dates, add or subtract days, weeks, months or working days, and find the day of the week for any date. Free, with holidays.

### At a glance

- Counts the **days between two dates** and shows them as years, months and days, weeks, hours, minutes and seconds.
- Counts **working days** with your own weekend — Saturday–Sunday, Sunday only, Friday–Saturday or Friday only — and skips the **holidays** you add, including India’s national holidays in one tap.
- **Adds or subtracts** years, months, weeks and days from any date, or a number of **working days** for notice periods and deadlines.
- Finds the **day of the week** for any date from year 1 to 9999, with the day of the year, ISO week number, quarter and a month calendar.
- Handles month ends the way people expect: 31 January plus one month is 28 (or 29) February.
- Choose whether to **include the end date** — on for leave and events, off for nights and deadlines.

### Features

- **Days between dates**: In days, weeks, months and years, and in hours and seconds.
- **Working days**: Any weekend pattern, with holidays skipped.
- **Add or subtract**: Years, months, weeks, days or working days.
- **Day of the week**: For any date from year 1 to 9999.
- **Week number**: ISO 8601 week, day of the year and quarter.
- **Private**: Runs in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.

### How to count the days between two dates

1. **Pick the start date** — Choose the first date, or tap Today.
2. **Pick the end date** — Choose the second date. The order doesn’t matter.
3. **Include the end date?** — Turn it on to count both the first and the last day.
4. **Read the result** — The total days appear at once, with weeks, months, working days and weekend days.

### Guide

#### Should I include the end date?

From Monday to Friday is **4 days** if you count the gaps between dates — the usual answer for ages, deadlines, loan interest and hotel nights. It is **5 days** if you count every calendar day you are away — as for leave, a festival or a course. Turn on **Include the end date** for the second kind.

#### Common date questions

| Question | Use |
| --- | --- |
| How many days until my exam / wedding / trip? | Days between dates, start = Today |
| What is the date 90 days from today? | Add or subtract → + 90 days |
| When does a 30-day notice period end? | Add or subtract → 30 days (or working days) |
| How many working days are in this month? | Days between dates, end date included |
| What day of the week was I born? | Day of the week |
| Which week number is it? | Day of the week → Week number (ISO) |

#### How months are counted

Months have 28 to 31 days, so “one month later” keeps the same day of the month when it exists and otherwise moves to the last day: 31 January + 1 month = 28 February (29 in a leap year), and 31 March − 1 month = 28 or 29 February. The years-months-days split counts whole months first and then the days left over, as an age is counted.

### FAQ

**How do I calculate the number of days between two dates?**
Enter both dates under **Days between dates**. The calculator subtracts them using the calendar, counting leap years correctly, and shows the result in days, weeks and years-months-days.

**Does it count leap years?**
Yes. A year is a leap year if it divides by 4, except century years, which must divide by 400 — so 2000 and 2024 were leap years and 1900 was not.

**How are working days counted?**
Every day in the range except your weekend days and the holidays you add. Holidays that fall on a weekend are not subtracted twice.

**Can I use a six-day working week?**
Yes. Choose **Sunday only** as the weekend. For the Gulf, choose **Friday and Saturday**.

**What day of the week was 15 August 1947?**
A Friday. Pick any date under **Day of the week** to see its weekday, day of the year and week number.

**What is an ISO week number?**
Weeks start on Monday, and week 1 is the week containing the year’s first Thursday. Most of Europe and many planners use it; a year has 52 or 53 ISO weeks.

### How to generate a random number

2. **Choose how many** — Ask for one number or many. Turn on No repeats for unique numbers.
3. **Press Generate** — The number appears at once. Copy or download a list of many numbers.
4. **Or draw one by one** — Use Draw one by one for raffles and housie — each number comes up only once.

### Guide

#### Is it really random?

Ordinary random functions in programming languages follow a formula that can be predicted. This generator uses **crypto.getRandomValues**, the browser’s cryptographically secure generator that is fed by your device’s hardware, and it **rejects the uneven remainder** of each draw so that no number is even slightly more likely than another. That makes it suitable for prize draws and classroom picks; for an official lottery, use the method its rules require.

| Housie / tambola calling | Draw one by one → Housie 1–90 |
| A random PIN | 4-digit PIN preset (0000–9999) |
| Split a class into groups | 1 to the number of groups, as many numbers as students |

### FAQ

**How do I pick a random number between 1 and 100?**
Tap the **1–100** preset (or type 1 and 100) and press **Generate**. Every number from 1 to 100 has the same 1-in-100 chance.

**Can I get random numbers without repeats?**
Yes. Turn on **No repeats** and ask for as many numbers as you need — up to the size of the range. For a live draw, use **Draw one by one**.

**Can I use it for housie or tambola?**
Yes. Choose **Draw one by one → Housie 1–90** and press Draw next for each number. The board shows every number called, you can undo a mistake, and the draw is kept if the page reloads.

**Can I generate decimal numbers?**
Yes. Choose 1 to 6 decimal places; for example 0 to 1 with 2 places gives numbers such as 0.37.

**Can I leave some numbers out?**
Yes. Type them under **Leave out**, such as 13 or 20-25, and they will never be picked.

**Is it free and private?**
Yes. It is free, needs no sign-up, and runs entirely in your browser; your settings and any draw in progress are remembered on this device only.

- **Line, word or character**: Pick the level of detail that suits code, documents or single words.
- **Changed words highlighted**: Edits within a line are marked, not just the whole line.
- **Side by side or inline**: Two columns on a wide screen, one on a phone.
- **Fold unchanged lines**: Only the changes and a few lines around them.
- **Smart matching**: The same algorithms git uses: patience and Myers diff.
- **Private**: Nothing is uploaded; large files compare in a moment.

### How to compare two texts

1. **Paste the original** — Paste or type the first version on the left, or open a file.
2. **Paste the changed version** — Paste the second version on the right.
3. **Read the differences** — Red shows what was removed, green what was added, and highlighted words what changed inside a line.
4. **Adjust and export** — Ignore case or spaces, switch views, and copy or download the differences as a .diff file.

### Guide

#### Reading the result

| You see | It means |
| --- | --- |
| Red line (−) | The line is only in the original — it was removed. |
| Green line (+) | The line is only in the changed text — it was added. |
| Red and green line side by side | The line was changed; the highlighted words are the edits. |
| “Show 12 unchanged lines” | Identical lines folded away — click to show them. |

#### Lines, words or characters?

**Lines** suits code, lists, CSV and most documents: each line is matched as a whole, then the changed words inside are highlighted. **Words** suits paragraphs of prose, where one edit can reflow a whole line. **Characters** suits short strings such as IDs, URLs, passwords or spelling, where a single letter matters.

#### How the comparison works

The texts are split into lines (or words, or characters), and the smallest set of additions and removals that turns one into the other is found with Eugene Myers’ diff algorithm. For long files, lines that appear exactly once in both versions are matched first — the “patience” method used by git — which keeps moved blocks and repeated lines like “}” from producing confusing results.

### FAQ

**How do I find the difference between two texts?**
Paste the original on the left and the new version on the right. The differences appear immediately: removed lines in red, added lines in green and changed words highlighted.

**Is my text uploaded anywhere?**
No. The comparison runs entirely in your browser, so it is safe for contracts, code and personal documents. The text is not saved; only your view settings are remembered.

**Can I compare code?**
Yes. Line mode with side-by-side view works like a code review, and you can download a unified .diff file to apply with git apply or patch.

**Can I compare Word or PDF files?**
Copy the text out of the document and paste it here. For PDFs, the Compare PDF tool compares two PDF files page by page.

**How do I ignore differences in spacing or capital letters?**
Turn on **Ignore spaces** (extra spaces, tabs and trailing spaces) or **Ignore case** (capital and small letters are treated as the same).

**How large can the texts be?**
Files of tens of thousands of lines compare in about a second. Character-by-character comparison switches to words for very long texts.

- In **Hindi** too — “बारह लाख चौंतीस हज़ार …” — with अरब and खरब for very large numbers, and the amount as “… रुपये … पैसे मात्र”.

3. **Pick the style** — Title Case is usual for cheques; switch hyphens or “Only” on or off.

### Guide

#### Writing the amount on a cheque

Write the amount in words on the line after “Rupees”, starting as far left as possible, and end with **Only** so nothing can be added afterwards: for ₹25,500 write “Twenty Five Thousand Five Hundred Only”. With paise, write “… and Fifty Paise Only”. The amount in words must match the figures in the box; if they differ, banks usually return the cheque.

#### Indian and international number systems

| Number | Indian system | International system |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1,00,000 / 100,000 | One lakh | One hundred thousand |
| 10,00,000 / 1,000,000 | Ten lakh | One million |
| 1,00,00,000 / 10,000,000 | One crore | Ten million |
| 10,00,00,000 / 100,000,000 | Ten crore | One hundred million |
| 1,00,00,00,000 / 1,000,000,000 | One hundred crore (one arab) | One billion |

#### Number names in Hindi

| Number | हिंदी | Hindi (Roman) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1,000 | एक हज़ार | ek hazaar |
| 1,00,000 | एक लाख | ek lakh |
| 1,00,00,000 | एक करोड़ | ek crore |

| 1,00,00,00,00,000 | एक खरब | ek kharab |

### FAQ

**How do I write 1,50,000 in words?**
One lakh fifty thousand. As a cheque amount: “Rupees One Lakh Fifty Thousand Only”. In the international system it is one hundred fifty thousand.

**How do I write an amount with paise in words?**
Write the rupees, then “and”, then the paise: ₹1,234.50 is “Rupees One Thousand Two Hundred Thirty Four and Fifty Paise Only”.

**Should I write “lakh” or “lakhs”?**
Use the singular after a number: “five lakh”, “two crore”, just as you would write “five thousand”. That is the form used in official writing and on cheques.

**What is 10 lakh in millions?**
10 lakh is 1 million (10,00,000 = 1,000,000), and 1 crore is 10 million. Type “10 lakh” to see both systems.

**Can it write numbers in Hindi?**
Yes — every number appears in Hindi words, for example 12,500 = बारह हज़ार पाँच सौ, and amounts as “… रुपये … पैसे मात्र”.

**How large a number can it convert?**
Up to 36 digits — beyond a lakh crore in the Indian system and up to decillions internationally — exactly, with no rounding of the whole part.

## CSS Gradient Generator

URL: https://justtools.online/css-tools/css-gradient-generator/
Category: CSS Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Make beautiful CSS gradients: linear, radial and conic, smooth OKLCH blending, drag-and-drop colour stops, Tailwind classes and PNG wallpapers. Free.

### At a glance

- **Linear, radial and conic** gradients, with **repeating** stripes and rings.
- Drag colour stops along a bar, click to add one, and set each stop’s **colour, opacity and position**.
- Blend colours in **OKLCH or OKLab** for vivid, even gradients without the grey middle of classic sRGB — with an automatic fallback for older browsers.
- Copy ready-made **CSS**, **Tailwind CSS v4 classes** or **gradient text** CSS.
- Download the gradient as a **PNG** in Full HD, 4K, square or phone sizes — for wallpapers, slides and posts.
- Twelve presets, a **random** button and a reverse button to get started fast. Everything runs in your browser.

### Features

- **Three kinds**: Linear, radial and conic, repeating or not.
- **Drag-and-drop stops**: Up to 16 stops with colour, opacity and position.
- **Smooth blending**: OKLCH and OKLab interpolation, with an sRGB fallback.
- **Tailwind ready**: v4 gradient utilities, checked against Tailwind itself.
- **Gradient text**: Preview and copy CSS for gradient-coloured headings.
- **PNG wallpapers**: Up to 4K, painted at full resolution.

### How to make a CSS gradient

1. **Pick a starting point** — Choose a preset, press Random, or start from the default.
2. **Edit the colour stops** — Click the bar to add a stop, drag stops to move them, and choose each colour and its opacity.
3. **Set the type and direction** — Choose linear, radial or conic and turn the angle dial — or tap the preview to move a radial centre.
4. **Copy the code** — Copy the CSS or Tailwind classes, or download a PNG.

### Guide

#### Linear, radial and conic gradients

| Type | What it looks like | CSS |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linear | Colours change along a straight line at any angle. | linear-gradient(135deg, …) |
| Radial | Colours spread out from a centre as a circle or ellipse. | radial-gradient(circle at 50% 30%, …) |
| Conic | Colours sweep around a centre, like a colour wheel or pie chart. | conic-gradient(from 0deg, …) |
| Repeating | The stops repeat to make stripes, rings or rays. | repeating-linear-gradient(…) |

#### Why OKLCH gradients look better

Browsers used to blend gradient colours in sRGB, the same space that stores the colours. Mixing blue and yellow that way passes through grey, and red to blue goes through a dull purple. **OKLCH** and **OKLab** are colour spaces built around how we see brightness and colour, so the middle of the gradient stays bright and saturated. CSS has supported `in oklch` since 2023 (Chrome 111, Safari 16.2, Firefox 127); the generated CSS includes an sRGB version first, with extra in-between stops, so older browsers show nearly the same result.

### FAQ

**How do I add a gradient background in CSS?**
Use `background: linear-gradient(135deg, #7f5af0 0%, #e45fd0 100%);` on the element. Design it here and press Copy to get the exact code.

**How do I make a gradient in Tailwind CSS?**
In Tailwind v4 use `bg-linear-to-r from-[#7f5af0] to-[#e45fd0]` (or an angle such as `bg-linear-65`), with `via-` for a middle colour. The Tailwind tab gives these classes; gradients with more stops become an arbitrary `bg-[…]` value.

**How do I make gradient text?**
Give the text a gradient background, then clip it to the text: `background-clip: text; color: transparent;`. Switch the preview to Text and copy the Gradient text tab.

**Can I use transparency in a gradient?**
Yes. Lower a stop’s opacity to fade to transparent — useful for overlays on photos. The preview shows a checkerboard behind transparent parts.

**Can I download the gradient as an image?**
Yes. Choose a size — up to 4K, square or phone — and press Download PNG.

**Do the gradients work in all browsers?**
Linear, radial and conic gradients work in every current browser. OKLCH blending needs a 2023 or newer browser; the CSS includes an sRGB fallback line for older ones.

| --- | --- |

#### Is an image of my signature legally valid?

A signature image is an **electronic signature**: many everyday documents — letters, quotes, internal approvals, delivery notes — accept it. Contracts and filings that require a **digital signature certificate** (DSC) or Aadhaar eSign in India, or a qualified signature elsewhere, need a certified signing service instead. When in doubt, ask the organisation that will receive the document.

#### Tips for a good signature image

Sign at your natural speed — the pen effect depends on it. On a phone, turn the screen sideways for a wider pad. For photo uploads, sign with a dark pen on plain white paper, photograph it straight on in daylight, and raise the sensitivity if grey shadows remain. Many government forms ask for a signature of a given size, such as 140 × 60 pixels and under 20 KB; use the Image Resizer and Image Compressor to match.

**Can I add my signature to a PDF?**
Yes. Press Save for Sign PDF, then open Sign PDF: your signature will be ready to place on any page.

**Is my signature stored anywhere?**
No. It is drawn and saved only in your browser. If you use Save for Sign PDF, it is kept in this browser so Sign PDF can use it; you can remove it there.

**Can I type my signature in Hindi?**
Yes. Type your name in Devanagari and choose the Hindi + English style.

**What size should a signature image be for online forms?**
Each portal sets its own rules — often around 140 × 60 pixels and 10–20 KB, in JPG. Download the JPG on white here, then use the Image Resizer and Image Compressor to match exactly.

## GSTIN, PAN & Aadhaar Validator

URL: https://justtools.online/business-tools/india-id-validator/
Category: Business Tools
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Check GSTIN, PAN, Aadhaar, IFSC, UPI ID, CIN, TAN and vehicle numbers for typos: check digits verified, every part explained, hundreds at once. Private.

### At a glance

- Checks **GSTINs** fully: the state code, the PAN inside, the registration number and the **check character** — the last character catches almost every typo.
- Checks **Aadhaar numbers and Virtual IDs** with the **Verhoeff** check digit, and shows the number masked.
- Explains **PAN** (holder type: person, company, HUF, firm…), **CIN** (listed or not, state, year, company type), **TAN**, **IFSC** (which bank) and **UPI IDs** (which app).
- Also checks **mobile numbers**, **PIN codes**, **vehicle numbers** (including BH series), **passport** and **voter ID** numbers.
- **Bulk mode**: paste a column of up to 5,000 numbers from Excel, see which are wrong, and download the results as CSV.
- Runs entirely in your browser — numbers are **never uploaded or saved**.

### Features

- **12 kinds of numbers**: Detected automatically from their shape.
- **Real check digits**: GSTIN check character and Aadhaar Verhoeff digit.
- **Every part explained**: State, holder type, bank, app, company type and more.
- **Bulk checking**: Thousands of lines from a spreadsheet, with CSV export.
- **Official links**: Where to confirm a number is real and active.
- **Private**: Checked on your device; nothing leaves it.

### How to check a GST number

1. **Paste the GSTIN** — Type or paste the 15-character GST number. The type is detected automatically.
2. **Read the result** — A valid format shows the state, the PAN and each part of the number; a typo shows exactly what is wrong.
3. **Check many at once** — Switch to Many at once and paste a column from your vendor list or invoice register.
4. **Confirm it is active** — For a supplier, use the GST portal’s Search Taxpayer to see the legal name and status.

### Guide

#### How a GSTIN is built

| Characters | Meaning | Example (27AAPFU0939F1ZV) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1–2 | State code | 27 = Maharashtra |
| 3–12 | PAN of the business | AAPFU0939F |
| 13 | Registration number under that PAN in the state | 1 = first |
| 14 | Letter Z by default | Z |
| 15 | Check character, calculated from the first 14 | V |

#### The 4th letter of a PAN

| Letter | Holder |
| --- | --- |
| P | Individual |
| C | Company |
| H | Hindu Undivided Family |
| F | Firm or LLP |
| A / B | Association of Persons / Body of Individuals |
| T | Trust |
| G / L / J | Government / Local authority / Artificial juridical person |

#### Valid format is not the same as genuine

A correct check digit proves the number has no typing mistake — not that it was issued to anyone, or is still active. Anyone can make up a number that passes. Before paying a supplier or accepting a document, confirm it with the issuing authority: the GST portal for GSTINs, the Income Tax e-filing portal for PANs, UIDAI for Aadhaar and MCA for companies. Never share someone’s full Aadhaar number without need; use the masked form.

### FAQ

**How do I check if a GST number is valid?**
Paste it above. The tool checks the 15-character format, the state code and the check character, which catches nearly all typos. To see the business name and whether the registration is active, use Search Taxpayer on the GST portal.

**Can it tell me whose PAN or Aadhaar this is?**
No. Names are held only by the Income Tax Department and UIDAI, and this tool never contacts them. It checks the format and explains what the characters mean.

**Is it safe to enter Aadhaar numbers here?**
The check runs entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded, stored or logged — and the result is shown masked. Still, share Aadhaar numbers only when you have to.

**What is the Verhoeff algorithm?**
A check-digit formula that detects every single-digit mistake and every swap of two neighbouring digits. The last digit of an Aadhaar number is a Verhoeff check digit.

**Can I validate a whole list from Excel?**
Yes. Choose Many at once, paste the column, and download the results as CSV with the reason for every invalid number.

**Does a PAN have a check digit?**
Yes, the last letter — but the Income Tax Department has not published the formula, so only the format and the holder-type letter can be checked.

- **UPI built in**: Pay links and QR codes with the amount filled in.
- **Share anywhere**: WhatsApp summary, a link or a CSV.
- **Mark as paid**: Record payments as friends settle up.
- **Private**: No account; stored only on your device.

### How to split expenses with friends

1. **Add the people** — Type everyone’s name, and their UPI ID if you want pay links.
2. **Add each expense** — Enter what it was, the amount and who paid, and choose who shares it and how.
3. **Check the balances** — Green shows who gets money back, red who owes.
4. **Settle up** — Follow the short payment list — tap Pay with UPI or scan the QR — and share it on WhatsApp.

### Guide

#### An example

Four friends go to Goa. Asha pays ₹12,000 for the hotel, Ravi ₹2,400 for scooters, and Meena ₹3,600 for a dinner that Kabir skipped. The total is ₹18,000. Each owes ₹3,600 for the hotel and scooters, and the three at dinner owe ₹1,200 each for it. So Asha gets ₹7,200 back, while Ravi owes ₹2,400, Meena ₹1,200 and Kabir ₹3,600 — three payments to Asha instead of a tangle of small ones.

#### Ways to split a bill

| Split | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| Equally | Hotel, cab, groceries — everyone pays the same. |
| Exact amounts | Restaurant bills where each person ordered different things. |
| Shares | Families and children: 2 shares for a couple, 1 for a child, ½ for a toddler. |
| Percent | Rent split by room size, such as 40% / 30% / 30%. |

### FAQ

**How does it decide who pays whom?**
It works out each person’s balance (what they paid minus their share), pairs people who owe and are owed the same amount, then has the biggest debtor pay the biggest creditor until everyone is even. That keeps the number of payments small.

**How do UPI payments work here?**
Add the UPI ID of the person being paid. Their settle-up line then has a Pay with UPI link (opens your UPI app on a phone) and a QR code to scan from another phone, with the amount and a note filled in. The payment itself happens in your UPI app.

**Can my friends see the expenses?**
Use Copy link or Share on WhatsApp: the link contains the whole trip, so it opens on any phone without an account. Nothing is uploaded to a server.

**What if someone paid part of what they owe?**
Press Mark as paid after a payment, or add an expense paid by them and shared only by the person they paid. The balances update at once.

**Does it round correctly?**
Yes. Amounts are kept in paise, and any leftover paisa from an uneven split goes to one person, so every split adds up exactly to the bill.

**Is it free?**
Yes, with no limits, no sign-up and no app to install.

## Solar Rooftop Calculator

Find the right rooftop solar size for your bill, the cost after the PM Surya Ghar subsidy, monthly savings, payback and 25-year savings for your state.

### At a glance

- Sizes a rooftop system from your **monthly bill or units**, using typical sunshine for **your state**, and checks it fits your **roof**.
- Works out the **PM Surya Ghar** central subsidy for homes: ₹30,000 per kW for the first 2 kW and ₹18,000 for the 3rd — up to **₹78,000** (10% more in special-category states).
- Shows the **monthly saving**, the **payback period** and **25-year savings**, counting panel ageing, rising tariffs and surplus units sold back under **net metering**.
- Compares the monthly saving with a **loan EMI**, so you can see whether solar pays its own instalments.
- Every assumption — cost per kW, units per kW, export price, tariff rise — is shown and can be changed.

### Features

- **Subsidy built in**: PM Surya Ghar slabs, with special-category states.
- **Real payback**: Panel ageing, tariff rises and net metering included.
- **Loan check**: EMI against your monthly saving.
- **Your numbers**: Change any assumption to match your quote.
- **25-year view**: Chart and table of savings, year by year.

### How to calculate rooftop solar for your home

1. **Choose your state** — It sets how many units each kW of panels produces where you live.
2. **Enter your bill** — Your average monthly bill (or units) and the price per unit.
3. **Add your roof area** — Optional — the shade-free area where panels can go.
4. **Read the result** — The recommended size, cost after subsidy, monthly saving and payback. Adjust the assumptions to match a vendor’s quote.

### Guide

#### PM Surya Ghar subsidy for homes

*North-eastern states including Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh, Andaman and Nicobar, and Lakshadweep. The subsidy is for residential connections, installed by a registered vendor and applied for on the national portal (pmsuryaghar.gov.in). Some states add their own subsidy on top.

| System size | Central subsidy | Special-category states* |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 kW | ₹30,000 | ₹33,000 |
| 2 kW | ₹60,000 | ₹66,000 |
| 3 kW or more | ₹78,000 | ₹85,800 |

#### How much does a home solar system produce?

In most of India, 1 kW of panels produces about 3.5 to 4.5 units a day — roughly 110 to 140 units a month — more in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Ladakh, less in the cloudy north-east. So a home using 300 units a month needs about 2.5 kW, which takes around 250 sq ft of shade-free roof. Panels lose about 0.5% of their output each year and usually come with a 25-year performance warranty.

### FAQ

**What size solar system do I need?**
Divide your monthly units by about 120 (what 1 kW produces in a month in much of India). 360 units a month needs about 3 kW. The calculator uses your state’s sunshine for a closer figure.

**How much does a 3 kW solar system cost after subsidy?**
At about ₹60,000 per kW, a 3 kW system costs around ₹1,80,000; the PM Surya Ghar subsidy of ₹78,000 brings it to about ₹1,02,000. Quotes vary with panel brand, inverter and roof structure — enter yours to see the payback.

**How long does rooftop solar take to pay back?**
Usually 3 to 6 years for a home with the subsidy, depending on your tariff, sunshine and how much of the power you use yourself. The panels then keep saving for 20 years or more.

**What happens to the units I don’t use?**
With net metering, surplus units go to the grid and are credited on your bill — often at a lower rate than you pay. Change the price for surplus units to match your state’s rules.

**Is the subsidy available for shops or offices?**
No — PM Surya Ghar is for homes (and housing societies for common areas). Turn off the subsidy to see the numbers for a commercial roof.

**Does it include batteries?**
No. Most homes use on-grid systems without batteries; the grid acts as storage under net metering. Batteries add cost and are not covered by the subsidy.

### How to make rent receipts for HRA

### Guide

#### What employers check on rent receipts

| Item | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Tenant and landlord names | The rent must be paid by you to the owner (paying rent to a parent is allowed if they own the house and declare the income). |
| Property address | It should match the address you declare for HRA. |

| Landlord’s PAN | Required when the yearly rent is above ₹1,00,000; if the landlord has none, a declaration from them is needed instead. |
| Landlord’s signature | Proves the rent was received. |
| Revenue stamp | For receipts paid in cash above ₹5,000. |

#### HRA in the new and old tax regimes

The HRA exemption is available only under the **old tax regime**. Under the new regime, which is the default, rent receipts don’t reduce your tax — but many employers still collect them during the year. Use the Income Tax Calculator to see which regime saves you more.

### FAQ

**Are rent receipts made online valid for HRA?**
Yes. Employers need the details — names, address, amount, period, the landlord’s PAN where required — and the landlord’s signature. A printed receipt signed by the landlord is accepted the same as a handwritten one.

**When is the landlord’s PAN required?**
When the rent you pay is more than ₹1,00,000 in the year (about ₹8,334 a month). If the landlord has no PAN, they give you a signed declaration saying so.

**Do rent receipts need a revenue stamp?**
Only receipts for cash payments above ₹5,000 need a ₹1 revenue stamp signed across by the landlord. Rent paid by UPI, bank transfer or cheque doesn’t.

**Monthly or quarterly receipts?**
Both are accepted by most employers. Quarterly receipts mean four signatures a year instead of twelve.

**Can I pay rent to my parents and claim HRA?**
Yes, if the house is owned by them, you really pay the rent (preferably by bank transfer), and they show it as income in their tax return.

**Is my information stored?**
Only in this browser, so the form is filled in next time. Nothing is uploaded.

## Gold Price Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/gold-price-calculator/

Last updated: 2026-10-23

Work out the real price of gold or silver jewellery: today’s rate, 22K or 18K purity, making charges, wastage, 3% GST and hallmarking, plus old gold exchange.

### At a glance

- Prices jewellery the way Indian jewellers bill it: **metal value + wastage + making charges + stones + hallmarking + 3% GST**.
- Enter the rate for **24K** and the calculator works out **22K, 20K, 18K or 14K** — or enter the rate for your purity directly. Silver too (999, 925).
- Making charges as a **percentage**, **per gram** or a **flat** amount, and weight in **grams, tola, pavan (sovereign) or ounces**.
- **Check a quote**: type the total a shop asked for, and see the making charge hidden in it.
- Value **old gold for exchange** from its pure-gold content at today’s rate, less the jeweller’s deduction — and what you pay after exchange.
- Remembers your rate and settings on this device. Everything is calculated in your browser.

### Features

- **Every karat**: 24K, 22K, 20K, 18K, 14K and silver.
- **Full bill**: Making, wastage, stones, hallmarking and GST.
- **Indian units**: Grams, tola, pavan and ounces.
- **Quote checker**: Find the making charge inside a total.
- **Old gold exchange**: Fair value at today’s rate.
- **Price per gram**: Compare shops on one number.

### How to calculate the price of gold jewellery

1. **Enter today’s rate** — Type the day’s rate for 24K gold (per 10 g is how it’s usually quoted) or the rate for your purity.
2. **Choose purity and weight** — Pick 22K, 18K or another purity, and enter the weight of the piece.
3. **Add the charges** — Enter the making charges, any wastage, stones and the hallmark fee. GST is 3%.
4. **Read the total** — See the full price, the price per gram and how much the making adds.

### Guide

#### The formula

**Price = (weight × rate for the purity) + making charges + wastage + stones + hallmarking, plus 3% GST on the total.** For 10 g of 22K gold when 24K is ₹7,000 a gram: the 22K rate is 7,000 × 916 ÷ 999 = ₹6,418.42 a gram, so the gold is worth ₹64,184.18. With 12% making charges (₹7,702.10) and ₹45 hallmarking, the total before GST is ₹71,931.29, and with 3% GST ₹74,089.22.

#### Gold purity

Hallmarked jewellery carries the BIS mark, the purity (such as 22K916) and a six-character HUID code that you can check in the BIS CARE app.

| Karat | Fineness | Gold content | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 24K | 999 | 99.9% | Coins and bars |
| 22K | 916 | 91.6% | Most Indian jewellery |
| 20K | 833 | 83.3% | Some traditional jewellery |
| 18K | 750 | 75% | Diamond and stone-set jewellery |
| 14K | 585 | 58.5% | Everyday and lightweight pieces |

### FAQ

**How are making charges calculated?**
Most jewellers charge a percentage of the gold value (often 8–25%), some charge a fixed amount per gram, and some add “wastage” or “value addition” as a percentage of the weight. Choose the method your jeweller uses — the result is the same price.

**What is the GST on gold jewellery?**
3% on the value of the jewellery including making charges. When you only pay for making (giving your own gold), a job worker charges 5% on the making.

**How do I convert the 24K rate to 22K?**
Multiply the 24K rate by 916 ÷ 999 (about 0.917). If 24K is ₹7,000 a gram, 22K is about ₹6,418 a gram. Many jewellers quote their own 22K rate — use that directly if you have it.

**How much is a tola or a pavan?**
A tola is 11.66 g and a pavan (sovereign) is 8 g. Choose the unit next to the weight.

**How is old gold valued for exchange?**
By its pure-gold content: weight × purity, at today’s rate, minus a deduction for melting and testing (usually 2–10%). Hallmarked gold is easier to value fairly.

**Does it show live gold rates?**
No — rates vary through the day and between cities. Enter the rate your jeweller or the day’s published rate shows; it’s remembered for next time.

## Gratuity Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/gratuity-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Calculate your gratuity with the 15/26 formula: years rounded the legal way, 5-year rule, fixed-term staff, the ₹20 lakh limit and the tax-free part.

### At a glance

- Uses the legal formula — **15 × last monthly basic + DA × years ÷ 26** — and shows it with your numbers.
- Counts years the way the law does: a part year of **more than six months counts as a full year**.
- Checks **eligibility**: five years of service, except on **death or disablement**, and **one year for fixed-term employees** under the labour codes.
- Applies the **₹20 lakh** maximum and splits the amount into **tax-free** and **taxable** parts — fully tax-free for government employees.
- Optionally applies the labour codes’ **50% wage rule**, which raises the wages used for gratuity when allowances are more than half of your pay.
- Also works for employers **not covered** by the Act (half a month’s wages per completed year), and shows what you’d get after more years.

### Features

- **Legal formula**: 15/26 under the Act, 15/30 otherwise.
- **Correct rounding**: More than six months counts as a year.
- **Eligibility check**: 5 years, death, and fixed-term staff.
- **Tax split**: Tax-free up to ₹20 lakh; all of it for government staff.
- **Labour codes**: The 50% wage rule, optional.
- **Dates or years**: Enter your joining and leaving dates or the service.

### How to calculate gratuity

1. **Enter your wages** — Your last monthly basic pay plus dearness allowance.
2. **Enter your service** — Years and months, or your date of joining and last working day.
3. **Choose the situation** — Whether your employer is covered by the Act, why you are leaving, and whether you are a government employee.
4. **Read the result** — The gratuity, the years counted, the formula with your numbers, and the tax-free part.

### Guide

#### The gratuity formula

**Gratuity = 15 × last drawn monthly wages × years of service ÷ 26.** “Wages” means basic pay plus dearness allowance. The 15 stands for fifteen days’ wages per year and the 26 for the working days in a month. With wages of ₹50,000 and 10 years’ service: 15 × 50,000 × 10 ÷ 26 = **₹2,88,462**. If your employer isn’t covered by the Act, gratuity is usually half a month’s wages per completed year: 50,000 × 10 ÷ 2 = ₹2,50,000.

#### How years of service are counted

| Service | Years counted (covered by the Act) |
| --- | --- |
| 6 years 5 months | 6 |
| 6 years 6 months | 6 |
| 6 years 7 months | 7 |
| 4 years 11 months | Not eligible yet (needs 5 years) |

#### The new labour codes

The Code on Social Security, 2020, which replaces the Payment of Gratuity Act under the new labour codes, keeps the same formula. It lets **fixed-term employees** get gratuity after one year, and the definition of wages means allowances above half of your total pay count as wages — so a low basic salary can no longer shrink your gratuity. Check your employer’s policy for how it applies these rules.

### FAQ

**Who is eligible for gratuity?**
Employees with at least five years of continuous service with the same employer, on resignation, retirement or termination. On death or disablement the five-year rule does not apply, and fixed-term employees qualify after one year.

**Do I get gratuity after 4 years and 240 days?**
Some High Courts have held that working at least 240 days in the fifth year completes five years of continuous service. Employers don’t all follow this, so check your company’s policy.

**Is gratuity taxable?**
For government employees it is fully tax-free. For others it is tax-free up to ₹20 lakh in a lifetime (or the formula amount, if lower); anything above is taxed as salary.

**What is the maximum gratuity?**
Under the law, ₹20 lakh. An employer can choose to pay more, but the amount above ₹20 lakh is taxable.

**Which salary is used — basic or gross?**
Basic pay plus dearness allowance. Under the labour codes, if your allowances are more than half of your total pay, the excess is added — turn on the 50% rule to see the effect.

**When must gratuity be paid?**
Within 30 days of it becoming payable. If it is late, the employer must pay simple interest on it.

## Morse Code Translator

URL: https://justtools.online/converters/morse-code-translator/
Category: Converters
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Translate text to Morse code and back, hear it at any speed, see it flash, download it as audio, and tap Morse yourself to decode it. Free and instant.

### At a glance

- Translates **both ways** as you type: text to International Morse code, and dots and dashes back to text — whichever box you type in.
- **Plays the code** with correct timing at 5–40 words per minute, with an adjustable tone and **Farnsworth spacing** for learning.
- Follow along as each symbol lights up, watch a **flashing lamp** (kept slow enough to be safe), or let your phone **vibrate** the code.
- Download the code as a **WAV audio file** for videos, puzzles and practice.
- **Tap Morse yourself** on a big key or the Space bar — it learns your speed and decodes what you send.
- A clickable **Morse alphabet** chart with letters, numbers and punctuation. Recognises **SOS**.

### Features

- **Two-way translation**: Text to Morse and Morse to text, live.
- **Real sound**: Correct timing from 5 to 40 WPM.
- **Farnsworth spacing**: Full-speed letters with longer gaps.
- **Light and vibration**: See the code or feel it on a phone.
- **Tap to decode**: Send Morse with a key; it adapts to your speed.
- **WAV download**: Save the code as audio.

### How to translate Morse code

1. **Type text or Morse** — Type words on the left, or dots and dashes on the right (use a space between letters and / between words).
2. **Read the translation** — The other box fills in as you type.
3. **Listen** — Press Play to hear it, and choose the speed and tone. Turn on the light or vibration if you like.
4. **Send your own** — Hold the tap key for dashes and tap quickly for dots — the decoder writes out what you sent.

### Guide

#### Morse code timing

Speed is measured in words per minute using the word PARIS, which takes exactly 50 units. At 20 WPM one unit lasts 60 milliseconds.

| Element | Length |
| --- | --- |
| Dot (dit) | 1 unit |
| Dash (dah) | 3 units |
| Gap inside a letter | 1 unit |
| Gap between letters | 3 units |
| Gap between words | 7 units |

#### Learning Morse code

Learn each letter as a sound, not as a picture of dots and dashes: listen to letters at a fairly high speed (15–20 WPM) with Farnsworth spacing, so the gaps give you time to recognise them, and shorten the gaps as you improve. Start with E, T, A, N, I and M, which are the shortest, and practise a little every day.

### FAQ

**What is SOS in Morse code?**
··· −−− ··· (...---...), sent as one continuous signal without letter gaps. It is the international distress signal.

**How do I type Morse code here?**
Use a full stop for a dot and a hyphen for a dash, a space between letters and a slash between words: .... .. / - .... . .-. . = HI THERE. The symbols ·, •, −, – and _ work too.

**What is Farnsworth spacing?**
Sending each letter at a high speed but leaving longer gaps between letters and words. It helps learners hear letters as whole sounds instead of counting dots.

**Can I decode Morse by tapping?**
Yes. Hold the key (or Space) for a dash and tap briefly for a dot; pause between letters and longer between words. The decoder works out your speed automatically.

**Is Morse code still used?**
Yes — by amateur radio operators, in aviation and marine navigation beacons, by people who communicate by tapping or blinking, and in puzzles and escape rooms.

**Does it work offline?**
Yes. Everything runs in your browser, including the sound.

### Guide

#### Before and after

select o.id, sum(i.qty*i.price) total from orders o join order_items i on i.order_id=o.id where o.status='paid' group by o.id order by total desc becomes a query with SELECT, FROM, JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY and ORDER BY each on their own line and their contents indented beneath — far easier to read, review and debug.

#### Common SQL style choices

| Choice | Why |
| --- | --- |
| UPPER-CASE keywords | Separates the SQL language from your table and column names at a glance. |
| One clause per line | Diffs and code reviews show exactly what changed. |
| AND / OR at line start | Easy to comment out or reorder conditions. |
| Tabular layout | Lines keywords up in a column, popular in data teams. |
| Minified | For embedding in code, logs, or URLs where whitespace gets in the way. |

### FAQ

**Is my SQL sent to a server?**
No. Formatting happens in your browser, so queries containing table names, customer data or credentials stay on your device.

**Which SQL dialect should I choose?**
The database you run the query on. Dialects differ in quoting ([name] in SQL Server, `name` in MySQL), operators (->> in PostgreSQL) and keywords; Standard SQL works for most simple queries.

**Why do I get a parse error?**
The formatter needs SQL it can read: check for an unclosed bracket or quote near the line shown, or try another dialect if the query uses database-specific syntax.

**Does it change what my query does?**
No. Only whitespace and the case of keywords change. Strings, quoted names and comments stay exactly as written (minifying removes comments).

**Can it format stored procedures and several statements?**
Yes — paste several statements separated by semicolons; each is formatted and separated by a blank line. Procedural code is formatted best with the matching dialect (T-SQL or PL/SQL).

**What library does it use?**
The open-source sql-formatter library (MIT licence) for formatting; minifying and colouring are our own.

## EPF Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/epf-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Calculate your PF: employee and employer contributions, the EPS split, interest at 8.25%, your EPF balance at retirement and an EPS pension estimate.

### At a glance

- Splits each month’s PF: **12% from you**, and the employer’s 12% divided into **8.33% for the pension (EPS, at most ₹1,250)** and the rest into your EPF.
- Projects your **EPF balance at retirement** with yearly salary rises, your current balance and the EPF interest rate — **8.25%** for 2023-24 and 2024-25, editable.
- Interest is worked out the EPFO way: on the **monthly running balance**, credited once a year.
- Estimates your **EPS pension**: pensionable salary × service ÷ 70, with two bonus years after 20 years of service.
- Handles **VPF** (voluntary contributions) and employers that cap PF at the ₹15,000 wage ceiling.
- A chart and a year-by-year table of your balance, contributions and interest.

### Features

- **Monthly split**: Employee, employer EPF and EPS shares.
- **Retirement corpus**: With salary rises and your current balance.
- **EPFO interest method**: Monthly running balance, credited yearly.
- **Pension estimate**: The EPS formula, with eligibility.
- **VPF and wage ceiling**: Extra contributions and capped PF.
- **Year by year**: Chart and table to retirement.

### How to calculate your EPF

1. **Enter basic pay + DA** — Your monthly basic salary plus dearness allowance — not gross or in-hand pay.
2. **Add age and raises** — Your age, retirement age and the yearly raise you expect.
3. **Add your balance** — Optionally, today’s EPF balance from your passbook.
4. **Read the result** — Your monthly contributions, the balance at retirement and your EPS pension estimate.

### Guide

#### Where your PF goes

With basic + DA of ₹30,000: you put in ₹3,600, the employer ₹3,600 — of which ₹1,250 goes to EPS and ₹2,350 to your EPF — so ₹5,950 a month reaches your EPF account.

| Contribution | Rate | Goes to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Employee | 12% of basic + DA | EPF (your account) |
| Employer — pension | 8.33% of wages up to ₹15,000 (max ₹1,250) | EPS (pension scheme) |
| Employer — rest | 12% minus the EPS share | EPF (your account) |
| Voluntary (VPF) | Any % you choose | EPF (your account) |
| EDLI and admin | Paid by the employer | Insurance and EPFO costs |

#### EPS pension

With at least 10 years of service, the pension from 58 is: pensionable salary (average of the last 60 months, at most ₹15,000) × pensionable service ÷ 70. Service of 20 years or more gets two extra years, and at most 35 years count — so the most this formula gives is ₹7,500 a month. The minimum pension is ₹1,000 a month.

### FAQ

**What is the EPF interest rate?**
EPFO declared 8.25% a year for 2023-24 and 2024-25. The rate is set every year, so change it in the calculator when a new rate is announced.

**How is EPF interest calculated?**
On the balance at the end of each month, at one-twelfth of the yearly rate, and credited to your account once a year. The calculator does the same.

**Why does only part of the employer’s share reach my EPF?**
8.33% of wages up to ₹15,000 — at most ₹1,250 a month — goes to the Employees’ Pension Scheme instead. It pays you a pension later rather than building your EPF balance.

**Is EPF tax-free?**
Contributions qualify for Section 80C in the old regime, and the balance is tax-free on withdrawal after five years of continuous service. Interest on your own contributions above ₹2.5 lakh a year (₹5 lakh if the employer doesn’t contribute) is taxable.

**Should I choose VPF?**
VPF earns the EPF rate with the same safety, which beats most fixed deposits, but the money is locked in until you leave or meet withdrawal rules. Keep it within the ₹2.5 lakh limit to keep the interest tax-free.

**How do I check my actual EPF balance?**
On the EPFO member passbook portal or the UMANG app with your UAN, or by a missed call or SMS to EPFO from your registered mobile number.

## Electricity Bill Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/electricity-bill-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Estimate your electricity bill from your appliances: units used by the AC, fridge, fans and geyser, slab tariffs, fixed charges, and where you can save.

### At a glance

- Add your appliances from a list of **30 common ones** — ACs, fridges, fans, geysers, TVs, pumps, EV chargers — with typical wattage, or your own.
- Works out **units (kWh) a month** for each: watts × how many × hours a day × days ÷ 1,000.
- Prices the units with **one rate** or your company’s **slab tariff** (each rate only on the units in its slab), plus fixed charges, duty and surcharges.
- Shows **what uses the most**, as a share of the bill — usually the AC, geyser or water pump.
- Suggests savings with real numbers: **BLDC fans**, **inverter ACs**, and the AC temperature.
- Your list and tariff are remembered on this device. Nothing is uploaded.

### Features

- **30 appliances**: Typical wattage, editable.
- **Units per appliance**: Hours a day and days a month.
- **Slab tariffs**: Telescopic slabs, fixed charges, duty.
- **Biggest users**: Share of the bill for each.
- **Saving tips**: BLDC fans, inverter AC, thermostat.
- **Remembers your home**: Saved on this device.

### How to calculate your electricity bill

1. **List your appliances** — Add each appliance, how many you have, and how long each runs a day.
2. **Enter your tariff** — Use one price per unit, or copy the slabs from your electricity company’s tariff.
3. **Add charges** — Fixed charge, electricity duty and any surcharge from your bill.
4. **Read the bill** — See the monthly units, the bill and which appliances cost the most.

### Guide

#### How to work out units

**Units (kWh) = watts × hours ÷ 1,000.** A 1,500 W AC running 8 hours uses 12 units a day — about 360 a month. A 75 W fan for 10 hours uses 0.75 units a day, or 22.5 a month. Fridges cycle on and off, so a typical double-door fridge averages about 60 W — some 43 units a month.

#### Typical monthly use

| Appliance | Use | Units a month |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.5-ton inverter AC | 8 hours a day | about 265 |
| Geyser 2,000 W | 1 hour a day | 60 |
| Double-door fridge | all day | about 43 |
| Ceiling fan | 10 hours a day | 22.5 (BLDC: about 10) |
| LED TV 32" | 5 hours a day | 6 |
| LED bulb 9 W | 6 hours a day | 1.6 |

### FAQ

**How many units does an AC use?**
A 1.5-ton inverter AC averages about 1–1.2 kW once the room is cool, so 8 hours a day uses roughly 8–10 units — 250–300 a month. A fixed-speed (non-inverter) AC uses about 30% more.

**How do slab tariffs work?**
Most Indian electricity companies charge more per unit as usage rises, and each rate applies only to the units inside its slab. With slabs of ₹3.50 up to 100 units and ₹6 for 101–300, using 150 units costs 100 × 3.50 + 50 × 6 = ₹650 in energy charges.

**Why is my real bill different?**
Hours of use vary day to day and by season, older appliances draw more, and bills add charges such as meter rent, fuel adjustment and taxes. Compare the units here with the units on your bill and adjust the hours.

**Does a TV or charger on standby use electricity?**
A little — usually 0.5–2 W each. Together, standby devices can add a few units a month; switching off at the socket avoids it.

**Are BLDC fans worth it?**
A BLDC fan uses about 30 W against 75 W for an ordinary fan. Running 10 hours a day, that saves about 13 units a month per fan, so it usually pays back in one to two years.

**Should I install solar panels?**
If your usage is high, compare with the Solar Rooftop Calculator, which sizes a system for your bill and includes the PM Surya Ghar subsidy.

A free Pomodoro timer for study and work: 25-minute focus sessions with breaks, tasks, a chime and notifications, and your daily focus time and streak.

### How to use the Pomodoro technique

2. **Focus for one Pomodoro** — Press Start and work on just that task until the chime — no phone, no tabs.
3. **Take a short break** — Stand up, stretch or get water for five minutes.

#### Why the Pomodoro technique works

The method, created by Francesco Cirillo in the late 1980s and named after his tomato-shaped kitchen timer, breaks work into short, fixed sessions. A deadline that is only 25 minutes away makes it easier to start and to resist distractions, and regular breaks keep you fresh for longer. Counting Pomodoros also shows how long tasks really take.

Pomodoro Technique® and Pomodoro™ are registered trademarks of Francesco Cirillo. This timer is not affiliated with or endorsed by him.

| Classic 25 / 5 | Most study and office work, and getting started on tasks you’ve been putting off. |
| Study 50 / 10 | Exam preparation and long reading once you’re used to focusing. |
| Deep work 90 / 20 | Writing, coding and problem-solving that needs long stretches. |
| Quick 15 / 3 | Younger students, low energy days, or tasks you dread. |

### FAQ

**What is a Pomodoro?**
One focus session — traditionally 25 minutes — followed by a short break. Four Pomodoros make a set, followed by a longer break.

**Does the timer keep running in another tab?**
Yes. It keeps time from the clock rather than counting seconds, so it stays exact in a background tab and even if you reload the page. Turn on the desktop notification to be told when a session ends.

**Can I change the session lengths?**
Yes. Choose a preset or Custom to set the focus, short break and long break lengths, and how often the long break comes.

**What happens if I skip a session?**
Skipped focus sessions don’t count towards your stats or tasks. Use Skip to jump straight to the next session.

**Is my data saved?**
Your settings, tasks and focus history are saved in this browser only. Clear history removes the stats.

**Is it free?**
Yes — no sign-up, no limits and no ads inside the timer.

## HRA Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/hra-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Work out tax-free HRA from basic pay, HRA and rent — with the 50% rule for 8 cities from FY 2026-27, month-by-month changes, and 80GG if you get no HRA.

### At a glance

- Applies the rule for **section 10(13A)**: tax-free HRA is the **least of** the HRA received, **rent minus 10% of salary**, and **50% of salary** in the big cities (**40%** elsewhere).
- From **FY 2026-27**, **Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune and Ahmedabad** are at 50% along with Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai. FY 2025-26 keeps the old list.
- Shows all three amounts and **which one limits you**, the **taxable HRA** and the **tax saved** at your slab.
- Handles a **raise, a move or a change of rent** mid-year: enter each month and the exemption is worked out month by month.
- Tells you the rent above which the exemption stops rising, and when your **landlord’s PAN** is needed (rent over ₹1 lakh a year).
- No HRA? Calculates the **section 80GG** deduction: the least of ₹5,000 a month, 25% of income, and rent minus 10% of income.

### Features

- **Three-rule check**: See which amount sets your exemption.
- **8 cities at 50%**: Rules for FY 2026-27 and 2025-26.
- **Month by month**: Raises, moves and rent changes.
- **Tax saved**: At 5%, 20% or 30% plus cess.
- **Section 80GG**: Rent deduction without HRA.
- **Rent receipts**: Make them with our receipt generator.

### How to calculate HRA exemption

1. **Enter your salary** — Your monthly basic pay plus dearness allowance, from your payslip.
2. **Enter HRA and rent** — The HRA you receive and the rent you pay each month.
3. **Choose the city** — Where you rent: it decides whether 50% or 40% of salary is the limit.
4. **Read the result** — Tax-free HRA for the year, the taxable part, and the tax it saves in the old regime.

### Guide

#### The HRA exemption formula

Tax-free HRA is the **lowest** of: (1) the HRA you actually receive, (2) rent paid minus 10% of salary, and (3) 50% of salary if you live in one of the eight big cities, or 40% anywhere else. “Salary” means basic pay plus dearness allowance (and commission fixed as a share of sales). With basic of ₹50,000 a month, HRA of ₹20,000 and rent of ₹25,000 in Mumbai: the amounts are ₹20,000, ₹20,000 and ₹25,000, so **₹20,000 a month — ₹2,40,000 a year — is tax-free**.

#### Which cities get 50%

The Income-tax Act, 2025 replaced the 1961 Act from tax year 2026-27 and the Income-tax Rules, 2026 added the four cities. Section numbers on this page are the familiar ones from the 1961 Act.

| City | FY 2025-26 | FY 2026-27 onwards |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai | 50% | 50% |
| Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad | 40% | 50% |
| Everywhere else | 40% | 40% |

### FAQ

**Can I claim HRA in the new tax regime?**
No. HRA exemption and the 80GG deduction are only available in the old regime. Compare both regimes with the Income Tax Calculator.

**Can I pay rent to my parents and claim HRA?**
Yes, if they own the house, you really pay the rent (ideally by bank transfer), and they show it as income in their tax return. Rent paid to your spouse is not accepted.

**When do I need my landlord’s PAN?**
When the rent is more than ₹1,00,000 a year — about ₹8,333 a month. If the landlord has no PAN, a signed declaration from them is needed.

**What if my salary changed during the year?**
The exemption is worked out for each period separately. Turn on “Salary, rent or city changed during the year” and enter each month.

**Can I claim both HRA and a home loan?**
Yes, if your own house is in a different city from where you work and rent, or you otherwise can’t live in it. Both benefits are in the old regime.

**I don’t get HRA. Can I still save tax on rent?**
Yes — section 80GG allows the least of ₹5,000 a month, 25% of total income and rent minus 10% of income, if neither you, your spouse nor minor child owns a house where you live or work.

## Calorie Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/calorie-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-23

Find your maintenance calories (TDEE), BMR and a daily target to lose or gain weight, with protein, fat and carbs, and a week-by-week path to your goal.

### At a glance

- Works out **resting energy (BMR)** with **Mifflin–St Jeor**, the revised **Harris–Benedict** or **Katch–McArdle** (from body fat), and your **maintenance calories (TDEE)** for five activity levels.
- Sets a **daily target** to lose 0.25–1 kg or gain up to 0.5 kg a week, using about **7,700 kcal per kg** of body weight.
- Warns when a target drops under **1,200 kcal (women)** or **1,500 kcal (men)**, or below your BMR.
- Splits the calories into **protein, fat and carbohydrate** for a balanced, high-protein or lower-carb diet, plus a **fibre** goal.
- Projects your weight **week by week** — recalculating your needs as you get lighter — and estimates the date you’ll reach your goal.
- Metric or US units; your details are remembered on this device only.

### Features

- **BMR and TDEE**: Three formulas, five activity levels.
- **Calorie target**: For a weekly loss or gain.
- **Safety checks**: Flags targets that are too low.
- **Macros**: Protein, fat, carbs and fibre.
- **Goal date**: A realistic week-by-week curve.
- **kg or lb**: Metric and US units.

### How to work out your daily calories

1. **Enter your details** — Sex, age, height and weight.
2. **Choose your activity** — From sedentary to extra active — be honest, most people overestimate.
3. **Pick a goal** — Keep your weight, or lose or gain a set amount a week, and your goal weight.
4. **Follow and adjust** — Eat around the target for 2–3 weeks, compare with your scale, and adjust by 100–200 kcal.

### Guide

#### How the calculation works

**BMR** is the energy your body uses at rest. The Mifflin–St Jeor formula is 10 × weight (kg) + 6.25 × height (cm) − 5 × age, plus 5 for men or minus 161 for women. Multiplying BMR by an activity factor (1.2 to 1.9) gives **TDEE**, the calories that keep your weight steady. A 30-year-old man of 70 kg and 175 cm has a BMR of about 1,649 kcal; if he exercises 3–5 days a week, his TDEE is about 2,556 kcal. To lose 0.5 kg a week he would eat about 550 kcal less: roughly **2,006 kcal a day**.

#### Activity levels

| Level | What it means | Factor |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sedentary | Desk job, little or no exercise | 1.2 |
| Lightly active | Light exercise 1–3 days a week | 1.375 |
| Moderately active | Exercise 3–5 days a week | 1.55 |
| Very active | Hard exercise 6–7 days a week | 1.725 |
| Extra active | Physical job, or training twice a day | 1.9 |

### FAQ

**How many calories should I eat to lose weight?**
About 500 kcal less than your maintenance calories loses roughly 0.5 kg a week. Losing 0.5–1% of your body weight a week is a sensible pace for most people.

**Which formula is the most accurate?**
For most adults, Mifflin–St Jeor. If you know your body fat percentage — for example from a DEXA scan — Katch–McArdle can be closer, especially for very muscular people.

**Why does weight loss slow down?**
As you lose weight, your body needs less energy, so the same intake makes a smaller deficit. The week-by-week chart includes this; recalculate every few kilos.

**How much protein do I need?**
At least 0.8 g per kg of body weight to stay healthy; 1.2–2 g per kg helps keep muscle while losing fat, especially with strength training.

**Is it safe to eat less than 1,200 calories?**
Not without medical supervision. Very low intakes make it hard to get enough nutrients and protein. Choose a slower goal or add activity instead.

**Does it work during pregnancy?**
No. Pregnancy and breastfeeding need extra energy and individual advice — please ask your doctor.

Free voice typing online: speak in Hindi, English or 20 other languages and get text, with spoken punctuation, auto-capitals, copy and download.

### How to type with your voice

2. **Press the microphone** — Allow microphone access the first time, then speak clearly at a normal pace.
3. **Say the punctuation** — Say “comma”, “full stop” or “new line” (“अल्पविराम”, “पूर्ण विराम”, “नई लाइन” in Hindi).
4. **Edit and save** — Fix any words by typing, then copy the text or download it.

### Guide

#### Which browsers support voice typing?

Recognition is done by the browser, not by this website. Chrome and Edge send the audio to Google’s or Microsoft’s speech service to turn it into text; the text then stays in your browser. We never receive your audio or your text.

| Browser | Voice typing |
| --- | --- |
| Chrome (computer, Android) | Yes — the most languages |
| Microsoft Edge | Yes |
| Safari (iPhone, iPad, Mac) | Yes |
| Firefox | No — use another browser |

#### Tips for better accuracy

Use a headset or sit close to the microphone, keep background noise down, and speak in full sentences at a steady pace. Choose the language you actually speak — for Hinglish, “Hindi” usually gives Devanagari and “English (India)” gives Roman script. Pause briefly before saying a punctuation word so it isn’t joined to the sentence.

### FAQ

**Is voice typing free?**
Yes — no sign-up, no time limit and no word limit.

**Can I type in Hindi by speaking?**
Yes. Choose Hindi and speak; the text comes out in Devanagari. Say “पूर्ण विराम” for । and “नई लाइन” for a new line.

**Why does it stop listening?**
Browsers end a recognition session after a pause or about a minute. The tool starts a new one automatically while the microphone button is on. If it keeps stopping, check that the microphone is allowed for this site.

**Is my voice recorded or stored?**
This website never receives your audio or text. Your browser’s speech service processes the audio to recognise it; the text is kept only in your browser until you clear it.

**Can it transcribe an audio file?**
No — it listens to the microphone live. To transcribe a recording, play it near the microphone, though accuracy will be lower.

**Does it work offline?**
Usually not: most browsers need an internet connection for speech recognition. Newer versions of Chrome can recognise some languages on the device.

## Color Contrast Checker

URL: https://justtools.online/css-tools/color-contrast-checker/

Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.

Check text and background contrast against WCAG AA and AAA, get the nearest passing colours, preview colour blindness, and test a whole palette at once.

### At a glance

- Calculates the **WCAG 2 contrast ratio** and checks **AA** and **AAA** for normal and large text, plus **3:1 for icons, borders and controls** (1.4.11).
- **Make it pass**: finds the nearest text or background colour that reaches AA or AAA — same hue, only lightness changes — and applies it in one click.
- Accepts **any CSS colour**: hex (with alpha), rgb(), hsl(), oklch(), lab() and names. Translucent colours are measured as they appear.

### Features

- **One-click fixes**: Nearest passing colour, same hue.
- **Any CSS colour**: Hex, rgb, hsl, oklch and names.
- **Live preview**: Text, link, button and border.
