### How to check colour contrast

1. **Enter the text colour** — Type any CSS colour or use the colour picker.
2. **Enter the background** — The colour behind the text.
3. **Read the result** — The ratio and which WCAG levels pass for normal text, large text and controls.
4. **Fix it** — If it fails, use a suggested text or background colour, or drag the lightness slider.

### Guide

#### WCAG contrast requirements

The ratio compares the relative luminance of the two colours, from 1:1 (the same) to 21:1 (black on white). Ratios are not rounded up: 4.49:1 fails AA. Logos, disabled controls and decorative text are exempt.

| What | AA | AAA |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal text | 4.5:1 | 7:1 |
| Large text (24px, or 18.66px bold) | 3:1 | 4.5:1 |
| Icons, borders, focus rings, chart lines | 3:1 | — |

#### Why only lightness changes

Contrast depends almost entirely on how light or dark the colours are. The suggestions keep your colour’s hue and adjust its lightness in the OKLCH colour space, so your blue stays blue — just darker or lighter — and the fix is as small as possible.

### FAQ

**What contrast ratio do I need?**
At least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text to meet WCAG AA, which most accessibility laws refer to. AAA asks for 7:1 and 4.5:1.

**Is grey text on white accessible?**
Only if it is dark enough. #767676 on white is 4.54:1 and passes AA; #777777 is 4.48:1 and fails.

**Does this use APCA?**
No. It uses the WCAG 2 formula, which current laws and audits are based on. APCA is still a draft for a future version of WCAG.

**How are transparent colours handled?**
Text with transparency is blended over the background, and a transparent background is blended over white, so the ratio matches what people see.

**Can I check colours in OKLCH or by name?**
Yes — anything your browser understands as a CSS colour, such as oklch(55% 0.15 250), lab(…) or rebeccapurple.

**Why does the colour-blind preview show the same ratio?**
Colour-vision deficiencies change hue far more than lightness, so the ratio barely moves. That is why lightness contrast — not colour — is what keeps text readable.

## Number Base Converter

URL: https://justtools.online/converters/number-base-converter/
Category: Converters
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-24

Convert between binary, decimal, hexadecimal, octal and any base from 2 to 36 — with the working shown, fractions, two’s complement and IEEE 754 floats.

### At a glance

- Converts between **binary, octal, decimal and hexadecimal** at once, plus any base from **2 to 36**.
- Exact for whole numbers of **any size** — hundreds of digits — and for **fractions**, where **repeating digits** are shown in brackets: 0.1 in binary is 0.0(0011).
- **Shows the working** the way it’s taught: place values to convert to decimal, **repeated division** (remainders read bottom-up) and **repeated multiplication** for fractions.
- Shows integers in **two’s complement** for 8, 16, 32 and 64 bits, and reads a binary pattern back as a signed number.
- Breaks a number into the **IEEE 754** sign, exponent and mantissa for 32-bit floats and 64-bit doubles, and shows the value actually stored.
- Accepts 0b, 0o and 0x prefixes, spaces and underscores, and groups digits for easy reading.

### Features

- **All bases at once**: Binary, octal, decimal, hex and base 2–36.
- **Step by step**: Division, multiplication and place values.
- **Fractions**: Exact, with repeating digits found.
- **Any size**: Big integers, no rounding.
- **Two’s complement**: 8, 16, 32 and 64 bits.
- **IEEE 754**: Float and double bits.

### How to convert between number bases

1. **Type the number** — Enter it in any base — 0x or 0b prefixes, spaces and underscores are fine.
2. **Choose its base** — Binary, octal, decimal, hexadecimal or another base from 2 to 36.
3. **Read every base** — The number appears in all the common bases at once; copy any of them.
4. **Follow the steps** — Pick a target base to see the division or multiplication working.

### Guide

#### How to convert decimal to binary

Divide the number by 2 again and again, writing down each remainder, until the quotient is 0. The remainders read **from the bottom up** are the binary number. For 13: 13 ÷ 2 = 6 r 1, 6 ÷ 2 = 3 r 0, 3 ÷ 2 = 1 r 1, 1 ÷ 2 = 0 r 1 — so 13 is **1101**. To go back, multiply each digit by its place value and add: 1×8 + 1×4 + 0×2 + 1×1 = 13. The same method works for any base: divide by 8 for octal, by 16 for hex.

#### Common values

| Decimal | Binary | Octal | Hex |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 | 1010 | 12 | A |
| 15 | 1111 | 17 | F |
| 16 | 1 0000 | 20 | 10 |
| 100 | 110 0100 | 144 | 64 |
| 255 | 1111 1111 | 377 | FF |
| 1024 | 100 0000 0000 | 2000 | 400 |

### FAQ

**How do I convert binary to decimal?**
Multiply each digit by 2 raised to its position (counting from 0 on the right) and add the results. 101101 = 32 + 8 + 4 + 1 = 45.

**How do I convert hex to decimal?**
Each hex digit is worth 16 times the one to its right; A–F stand for 10–15. 1F4 = 1×256 + 15×16 + 4 = 500.

**Why does 0.1 never end in binary?**
Only fractions whose denominator is a power of 2 end in binary. 0.1 = 1/10 repeats for ever (0.0001100110011…), which is why computers store 0.1 slightly inaccurately.

**What is two’s complement?**
The way computers store negative integers: invert all the bits of the positive number and add 1. In 8 bits, −1 is 11111111 and −128 is 10000000.

**What bases are supported?**
Any base from 2 to 36, using the digits 0–9 and then the letters a–z.

**Is there a size limit?**
No practical limit for whole numbers — conversion uses exact big-integer arithmetic. Fractions are shown up to 48 digits after the point.

## Retirement Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/retirement-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-24

Find the retirement corpus you need with inflation, what your savings and step-up SIP will reach, the extra SIP to close the gap, and how long it lasts.

### At a glance

- Works out the **corpus you need at retirement** to pay expenses that **rise with inflation every year**, until the age you plan for, while the rest keeps earning.
- Projects your **current savings** and a **step-up SIP** (raised every year) to retirement, month by month.
- Shows the **shortfall or surplus**, the **extra monthly SIP** — or **lump sum today** — that puts you on track.
- Tells you **until what age** your money lasts on the current plan.
- A chart of your money by age — growing while you work, then paying your expenses — with the on-track plan beside it, and a table view.
- Separate returns **before and after retirement**, since most people move to safer investments once they retire.

### Features

- **Corpus needed**: Inflation-adjusted, year by year.
- **Step-up SIP**: Raise your SIP every year.
- **Gap to close**: Extra SIP or a lump sum today.
- **Money lasts until**: The age your savings run out.
- **Two return rates**: Before and after retiring.
- **Chart by age**: Your plan and the on-track plan.

### How to plan your retirement corpus

1. **Enter your ages** — Your age now, when you want to retire, and how long the money should last — planning to 85 or 90 is sensible.
2. **Enter your expenses** — What you’d spend a month at today’s prices, and the inflation you expect.
3. **Enter your savings** — Money already saved for retirement, your monthly SIP and how much you’ll raise it each year.
4. **Read the plan** — The corpus you need, what you’ll have, and the extra SIP or lump sum that closes any gap.

### Guide

#### An example

A 30-year-old who spends ₹50,000 a month today and wants to retire at 60 will spend about **₹2.87 lakh a month** at 60 with 6% inflation. To pay that — rising every year — until 85, while earning 7% in retirement, they need about **₹7.48 crore** at 60. With ₹5 lakh saved and a ₹10,000 SIP raised 5% a year at 12%, they’d have about ₹6.17 crore: **₹1.31 crore short**, and the money would run out around 80. Investing about **₹2,800 more a month** (also raised 5% a year) closes the gap.

#### Rules of thumb

| Rule | What it says |
| --- | --- |
| 25–30 × yearly expenses | A corpus of about 25 to 30 times your first year’s expenses lasts a long retirement in India, where inflation is higher. |
| Start early | Each year of delay needs a noticeably bigger SIP, because the money has less time to compound. |
| Step up your SIP | Raising the SIP with your salary every year reaches the goal with a far smaller starting amount. |
| Keep health apart | Medical costs rise faster than inflation — hold health insurance and an emergency fund separately. |

### FAQ

**How much money do I need to retire in India?**
It depends on your expenses, inflation and how long you plan for. A common guide is 25–30 times your yearly expenses at retirement; this calculator works it out exactly for your numbers.

**What inflation should I assume?**
India’s consumer inflation has averaged around 5–6% a year; 6% is a reasonable planning figure. A higher figure gives a safer plan.

**What return should I expect?**
Diversified equity funds have returned around 10–12% a year over long periods, but with ups and downs. After retiring, a safer mix may earn 6–8%. Use conservative figures.

**Should I include EPF and PPF?**
Yes — add your current EPF, PPF and NPS balances to savings so far, and count your monthly contributions in the SIP.

**What is a step-up SIP?**
A SIP you raise every year, for example by 5–10% as your salary grows. It makes reaching a large corpus much easier.

**What if I retire early?**
Set the retirement age lower and plan until 90 or more. You’ll have fewer years to save and more years to fund, so the corpus needed rises sharply.

## Fuel Cost Calculator

Last updated: 2026-10-24

Work out the petrol or diesel cost of a trip and split it, compare the running cost of petrol, diesel, CNG and electric, and check your real mileage.

### At a glance

- **Trip cost**: fuel for the distance (one way or return), plus tolls and parking, and how much **each person pays**.
- **Petrol vs diesel vs CNG vs electric**: cost per km, per month and per year for the distance you drive, for a **car or two-wheeler**.
- Adds the **vehicle price** and **upkeep** to show the **total cost of owning** each over 3 to 10 years.
- Tells you **after how many km** a dearer CNG, diesel or electric vehicle **pays for itself** against petrol.
- Finds your **real mileage** with the full-tank method, and uses it in the other calculators.

- **Cost of owning**: Price + fuel + upkeep over the years.
- **Break-even**: When a pricier vehicle pays off.

### How to calculate fuel cost

1. **Enter the distance** — One way, and turn on Return trip if you’re coming back.
2. **Enter mileage and price** — Your vehicle’s km per litre (or kg, or kWh) and the fuel price in your city.
3. **Add tolls and people** — Tolls and parking, and how many people share the cost.
4. **Compare fuels** — Switch to Petrol vs CNG vs EV to see running and ownership costs for your monthly driving.

### Guide

#### The formula

**Fuel cost = distance ÷ mileage × fuel price.** A 500 km round trip in a car that does 15 km a litre needs 500 ÷ 15 = 33.3 litres; at ₹95 a litre that is about **₹3,167** — ₹6.33 a km. For an EV, use km per kWh and the electricity price: at 6.5 km/kWh and ₹8 a unit, the same trip costs about ₹615.

#### Petrol, diesel, CNG or electric? (car, 1,000 km a month)

Using example prices of ₹10 lakh (petrol), ₹11.5 lakh (diesel), ₹10.9 lakh (CNG) and ₹14 lakh (electric), with servicing included. Enter the actual prices of the models you’re comparing.

| Fuel | Typical cost a km | Fuel a month | Pays back the extra price after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Petrol (15 km/l at ₹95) | ₹6.33 | ₹6,333 | — |
| Diesel (19 km/l at ₹88) | ₹4.63 | ₹4,632 | about 1 lakh km |
| CNG (25 km/kg at ₹76) | ₹3.04 | ₹3,040 | about 28,000 km |
| Electric (6.5 km/kWh at ₹8) | ₹1.23 | ₹1,231 | about 71,000 km |

### FAQ

**How do I calculate petrol cost for a trip?**
Divide the distance by your car’s mileage to get the litres needed, then multiply by the price per litre. Add tolls and parking, and divide by the number of people sharing.

**Is an electric car cheaper to run than petrol?**
Charged at home, usually by far — around ₹1–1.5 a km against ₹6–7 for petrol. But EVs cost more to buy, so the saving takes a few years of regular driving to cover the extra price. Public fast charging costs more.

**Is CNG worth it?**
For people who drive a lot, often yes: CNG costs about half as much per km as petrol, and the extra price of a CNG car is usually recovered within 30,000 km or so. Boot space is smaller and filling stations fewer.

**How do I check my real mileage?**
Fill the tank to full and note the odometer. Drive normally; at the next fill-up, fill to full again and note how much went in and the new reading. Mileage = km driven ÷ litres filled.

**Why is my mileage lower than the company figure?**
Claimed (ARAI) figures come from standard test conditions. City traffic, AC, tyre pressure, load and driving style reduce real-world mileage by 15–30%.

**Does the ownership cost include insurance?**
No — it adds the vehicle price, fuel and upkeep. Insurance, resale value and an EV battery replacement are left out; they vary too much from model to model.

## Daily Panchang

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/panchang/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-24

Today’s Panchang for your city: tithi, nakshatra, yoga and karana with end times, Rahu Kaal, Abhijit Muhurat, day and night Choghadiya — in English or Hindi.

### At a glance

- The five limbs — **tithi**, **nakshatra** (with pada), **yoga**, **karana** and **vara** — at sunrise, each with the **time it ends** and what follows.
- The **Hindu month** in both systems — **purnimanta** (North India) and **amanta** (South and West) — with **adhik maas**, plus **Vikram** and **Shaka samvat**, ritu and ayana.
- **Sunrise, sunset, moonrise and moonset** for 400+ cities in India and abroad, in local time.
- **Rahu Kaal**, **Yamaganda** and **Gulika Kaal** to avoid, and **Abhijit** and **Brahma Muhurat**.
- **Day and night Choghadiya** — Amrit, Shubh, Labh, Char, Udveg, Kaal and Rog — with the one running now highlighted.
- Calculated in your browser with the **Lahiri (Chitrapaksha) ayanamsa** used by Indian almanacs; switch between English and Hindi.

### Features

- **Five limbs**: Tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana, vara.
- **End times**: When each changes, and to what.
- **Both month systems**: Purnimanta and amanta, adhik maas.
- **Muhurat**: Rahu Kaal, Abhijit, Brahma Muhurat.
- **Choghadiya**: Day and night, current one marked.
- **Any city, any date**: In English or Hindi.

### How to read today’s Panchang

1. **Choose your city** — Sunrise — and so every time in the Panchang — depends on where you are.
2. **Pick the date** — Today is shown first; use the arrows for the next or previous day.
3. **Read the five limbs** — The tithi, nakshatra, yoga and karana at sunrise, and when each ends.
4. **Check the timings** — Avoid Rahu Kaal for new work; use the Choghadiya to pick a good time.

### Guide

#### What the Panchang shows

| Element | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| Tithi | The lunar day: each 12° the Moon moves ahead of the Sun. 15 in the bright half (Shukla, to Purnima) and 15 in the dark half (Krishna, to Amavasya). |
| Nakshatra | Which of the 27 lunar mansions (13°20′ each) the Moon is in. |
| Yoga | One of 27, from the Sun and Moon longitudes added together. |
| Karana | Half a tithi — 11 karanas cycle through the month; Vishti (Bhadra) is avoided. |
| Vara | The weekday, counted from sunrise to sunrise. |

#### Rahu Kaal and Choghadiya

The daytime from sunrise to sunset is split into eight equal parts. **Rahu Kaal** is the 8th part on Sunday, 2nd on Monday, 7th on Tuesday, 5th on Wednesday, 6th on Thursday, 4th on Friday and 3rd on Saturday — so it moves with sunrise and is not a fixed clock time. **Choghadiya** divides the day and the night into eight periods each; Amrit, Shubh and Labh are good, Char is neutral (good for travel), and Udveg, Kaal and Rog are avoided.

### FAQ

**Why do Panchangs differ by a few minutes?**
Almanacs use slightly different methods for sunrise (the Sun’s centre or top edge, refraction) and positions. Differences of a few minutes are normal; this Panchang uses the Lahiri ayanamsa and the top edge of the Sun for sunrise.

**What is the difference between purnimanta and amanta months?**
Purnimanta months (used in North India) end on the full moon; amanta months (South and West India) end on the new moon. In the Shukla paksha both have the same name; in the Krishna paksha the purnimanta month is one ahead — Diwali falls in Kartika (purnimanta) or Ashwin (amanta).

**Which tithi is “today’s” tithi?**
Traditionally, the tithi running at sunrise applies to the whole day for most purposes. The Panchang also shows when it ends and which tithi follows.

**What should I avoid during Rahu Kaal?**
By tradition, starting new work, journeys and purchases. Routine work can continue.

**What is Abhijit Muhurat?**
The 8th of the 15 muhurtas of the day, around local noon, considered auspicious for most work — except on Wednesdays.

**Can I see the Panchang for another city or date?**
Yes — pick any of 400+ cities in India and abroad, and any date, past or future.

## Construction Material Calculator

URL: https://justtools.online/calculators/construction-calculator/
Category: Calculators
Processing: Runs entirely in the browser; user data is not uploaded.
Last updated: 2026-10-24

Work out bricks, cement bags, sand and aggregate for a brick wall, an RCC slab or column, or plaster — in feet or metres, with M20 mixes and material cost.

### At a glance

- **Brick wall**: number of bricks, cement bags and sand for a 9-inch or 4.5-inch wall, minus doors and windows, in 1:4, 1:5 or 1:6 mortar.
- **Concrete**: cement, sand, aggregate (gitti) and water for slabs, beams, columns and footings in **M10, M15, M20 or M25** nominal mix.
- **Plaster**: cement and sand for 12, 15 or 20 mm plaster on any area.
- Uses the standard site factors: dry volume = wet × **1.33** (brick mortar), × **1.54** (concrete), and plaster + 20% for joints then × 1.27; cement at 1,440 kg/m³ in **50 kg bags**.
- Sizes in **feet or metres**; sand and aggregate in **cubic feet, m³ and brass**.
- Add your local prices for an estimate of the **material cost**.

### Features

- **Bricks and mortar**: 9-inch and 4.5-inch walls.
- **Concrete mixes**: M10 to M25, any shape.
- **Plaster**: 12, 15 or 20 mm.
- **Feet or metres**: cft, m³ and brass.
- **Standard factors**: The ones engineers use.
- **Material cost**: At your local rates.

### How to calculate construction materials

1. **Choose the work** — A brick wall, concrete (slab, beam, column, footing) or plaster.
2. **Enter the sizes** — Length, height or width, and thickness — in feet or metres. Deduct doors and windows from walls.
3. **Pick the mix** — Mortar ratio for brickwork and plaster, or the concrete grade.
4. **Read the quantities** — Bricks, cement bags, sand and aggregate, and the cost at your rates.

### Guide

#### Quick reference (per cubic metre)

Plaster, 12 mm thick in 1:6 over 100 m² (about 1,076 sq ft), needs about 7.5 bags of cement and 1.57 m³ (55 cft) of sand. Figures exclude wastage.

| Work | Cement | Sand | Aggregate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Brickwork, modular bricks, 1:6 | 1.26 bags + about 500 bricks | 0.26 m³ (9.3 cft) | — |
| M15 concrete (1:2:4) | 6.3 bags | 0.44 m³ (15.5 cft) | 0.88 m³ (31.1 cft) |
| M20 concrete (1:1.5:3) | 8.1 bags | 0.42 m³ (14.8 cft) | 0.84 m³ (29.7 cft) |
| M25 concrete (1:1:2) | 11.1 bags | 0.39 m³ (13.6 cft) | 0.77 m³ (27.2 cft) |

#### How it’s worked out

Wet concrete is measured after compaction, but cement, sand and aggregate are bought loose, with air between the grains — so the dry volume is about 54% more (× 1.54). The dry volume is split by the mix: for M20 (1 : 1.5 : 3, 5.5 parts), cement is 1.54 ÷ 5.5 = 0.28 m³ per m³ of concrete, which is 0.28 × 1,440 ÷ 50 ≈ **8 bags**. Brick mortar uses × 1.33 because the mortar only fills the joints.

### FAQ

**How many bricks are in 1 m³ of brickwork?**
About 500 modular bricks (190 × 90 × 90 mm with 10 mm joints). With traditional 230 × 110 × 75 mm bricks it is about 400. Add around 5% for breakage.

**How many cement bags for 1 m³ of M20 concrete?**
About 8 bags (50 kg each) in a 1 : 1.5 : 3 nominal mix, with 0.42 m³ of sand and 0.84 m³ of aggregate.

**What is a brass?**
A measure used for sand and aggregate in many parts of India: 1 brass = 100 cubic feet (about 2.83 m³).

**Which mortar ratio should I use?**
1:6 is common for 9-inch walls and inner plaster, 1:4 for 4.5-inch walls and outer plaster. Follow your engineer’s specification.

**Does it include steel?**
No. Reinforcement depends on the structural design; ask your engineer for the bar schedule.

**Why does my contractor’s figure differ?**
Site practice, brick sizes, joint thickness, wastage and design mixes vary. Use this as a check and for ordering, not as a structural design.

## Rangoli & Mandala Maker

Draw a rangoli or mandala with 4- to 16-fold symmetry, fill it with colour like rangoli powder, or get a new design in one click. Download free as PNG.

### At a glance

- Every line you draw is repeated **4, 6, 8, 12 or 16 times** around the centre — with an optional **mirror** — so even a squiggle becomes a rangoli.
- **Fill colour** pours colour into a closed shape, like rangoli powder, in every symmetric copy at once.
- **Surprise me** creates a new design of petals, diamonds and dots in **Diwali, Marigold, Peacock, Pastel** or **Kolam (white)** colours — ready to colour or change.
- Choose the **floor** — terracotta, soil, slate, white or cream — and hide the guides when you’re done.

### Features

- **Symmetry drawing**: 4 to 16 segments, mirrored.
- **Colour fill**: Like rangoli powder.
- **Ready-made designs**: One click, five colour sets.
- **Floors**: Terracotta, white, slate…
- **Undo and erase**: Experiment freely.
- **PNG download**: With or without background.

### How to make a rangoli online

1. **Choose the symmetry** — 8-fold is classic; 12 or 16 gives finer, flower-like patterns.
2. **Draw or start from a design** — Draw petals and curves near the centre, or press Surprise me.
3. **Fill with colour** — Pick Fill colour and tap inside a shape — every copy fills together.
4. **Download** — Hide the guides and save your rangoli as a PNG to share or print.

### Guide

#### Rangoli, kolam and mandala

**Rangoli** is drawn on the floor at the entrance with coloured powder, rice, sand or flower petals for Diwali, Pongal, Onam and other festivals. **Kolam** (South India) and **muggulu** (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana) are usually white line patterns drawn around a grid of dots. **Mandalas** are circular designs with the same symmetry, used in art and meditation. All three are built from a pattern repeated around a centre — which is exactly what this tool does for you.

#### Tips for a beautiful design

Start with a small flower at the centre and work outwards in rings. Leave closed outlines so Fill colour has a shape to fill — a gap lets the colour leak out. Alternate warm and cool colours from ring to ring, and finish with white outlines or dots for the classic rangoli look. Print the design to use as a guide on the floor.

### FAQ

**Is the rangoli maker free?**
Yes — free, with no sign-up and no watermark.

**Why did the colour fill the whole background?**
The shape wasn’t fully closed. Undo, draw over the gap with the brush, and fill again.

**Can I print my rangoli?**
Yes. Download the PNG and print it; turn on Transparent background to print just the design.

**What is the best symmetry for a Diwali rangoli?**
8 with mirror is the classic choice. 6 suits star and lotus designs; 12 and 16 make intricate, mandala-like patterns.

**Does it work on a phone?**
Yes — draw with your finger, and use Fill colour to colour the shapes.

**Is my drawing saved?**
It stays in this page until you download it; reloading starts a new design. Your tool settings are remembered on this device.
